Something has also been said in the fourth book about the Sodomene salts, those produced in the so-called Dead Sea, and if anyone has read that book carefully, he will now need only a reminder, so that, once the gustatory quality has been stated, he may know the power of the drug.

Since, then, the salty quality at once disperses and draws together the substance that comes near it, the so-called aphronitron has its difference in this, insofar as in it one can clearly see only one prevailing flavour, which they call bitter, which has a dispersing power but does not have a contracting one, as salts do.

For salts consume all that is moist in bodies; and the remainder of the solid substance they draw together by their astringency, for which reason they also pickle, and keep free of putrefaction, the bodies of things that putrefy, which have a superfluous moisture and a substance that is loose (ἀδιάλυτον) and not compacted.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἁλῶν κεκαυμένων.] Ἅλες κεκαυμένοι τὸ μὲν διαφορητικὸν μᾶλλον ἔχουσι τῶν ἀκαύστων, εἰς ὅσον αὐτῶν λεπτομερέστερον γίγνεται τὸ σῶμα, τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς λαμβάνον δύναμιν, ὡς κᾀπὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἐδείχθη τῶν κεκαυμένων συμβαίνειν, οὐ μὴν ὁμοίως γε τοῖς ἀκαύστοις συνάγειν καὶ πιλοῦν τὴν στερεὰν οὐσίαν ἔτι δύνανται.
beads.english: On burnt salt.] Burnt salt has the dispersing property more than unburnt salt, to the extent that its body becomes more fine-particled, taking on its power from the fire, as was shown to happen in the case of the other burnt substances too; yet it is no longer able, in the same way as unburnt salt, to draw together and compact the solid substance.

greek_sentences: Περὶ ἁλῶν κεκαυμένων.] Ἅλες κεκαυμένοι τὸ μὲν διαφορητικὸν μᾶλλον ἔχουσι τῶν ἀκαύστων, εἰς ὅσον αὐτῶν λεπτομερέστερον γίγνεται τὸ σῶμα, τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ πυρὸς λαμβάνον δύναμιν, ὡς κᾀπὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἐδείχθη τῶν κεκαυμένων συμβαίνειν, οὐ μὴν ὁμοίως γε τοῖς ἀκαύστοις συνάγειν καὶ πιλοῦν τὴν στερεὰν οὐσίαν ἔτι δύνανται.

beads.greek: Περὶ νίτρου.] Νίτρον.
beads.english: On nitron.] Nitron.

beads.greek: ἐδείχθη καὶ τοῦτο τὸ φάρμακον ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ δύναμιν ἔχον ἁλῶν τε καὶ ἀφρονίτρου.
beads.english: This drug too was shown to have a power intermediate between salt and aphronitron.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἁλὸς ἄνθους.] Ἁλὸς ἄνθος, ἔνιοι μὲν ὡς ἓν ὄνομα τὸ ἁλόσανθον, ἔνιοι δὲ καὶ διαιροῦντες ἁλὸς ἄνθος ὀνομάζουσιν.
beads.english: On flower of salt.] Flower of salt: some people name it as a single word, halosanthon, while others divide it and call it flower of salt (halos anthos).

beads.greek: ἔστι δ’ ὑγρὸν τοῦτο τὸ φάρμακον λεπτομερέστερον καὶ τῶν κεκαυμένων ἁλῶν, δριμύ τε τῇ ποιότητι καὶ διαφορητικὸν ἱκανῶς τῇ δυνάμει.
beads.english: This drug is moist, more fine-particled even than burnt salt, pungent in quality and sufficiently dispersing in power.

beads.english: On froth of salt.] Froth of salt is a foam-like efflorescence of salt, being of a nature much more fine-particled than salt itself, so that it is able both to thin and to disperse much more than salt does, whereas it cannot contract the remainder of the substance as salt does.

beads.english: On asphalt.] Asphalt.

The power of the drug is drying and heating, in roughly the second order.
Reasonably, then, they use it for the agglutination of bloody wounds, and for the other conditions, all those that require to be dried together with a moderate heating.

beads.greek: Περὶ σπόγγου.] Σπόγγος ὁ μὲν κεκαυμένος δριμείας ἐστὶ καὶ διαφορητικῆς δυνάμεως.
beads.english: On sponge.] Sponge, when burnt, is of a pungent and dispersing power.

beads.greek: ἐχρῆτο δ’ αὐτῷ τις τῶν ἡμετέρων διδασκάλων καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐν ταῖς χειρουργίαις αἱμοῤῥαγίας, ἕτοιμον ἔχων ξηρὸν μὲν καὶ ἄνικμον, δεδευμένον δὲ μάλιστα μὲν ἀσφάλτῳ, μὴ παρούσης δὲ ταύτης πίττῃ, προσετίθει δ’ αὐτὸν τοῖς αἱμοῤῥαγοῦσι χωρίοις, ἔτι καιόμενον, ὡς ἐσχαροῦσθαί τε ἅμα τὸ μόριον καὶ οἷον πῶμά τι λαμβάνειν αὐτὸ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ καυθέντος σπόγγου.
beads.english: One of our teachers used it also for the haemorrhages that occur in surgical operations, keeping it ready, dry and devoid of moisture, soaked preferably in asphalt, or, if this was not at hand, in pitch; and he applied it to the bleeding places while it was still burning, so that the part was at once made to form an eschar and the body of the burnt sponge itself was received as a kind of stopper.

beads.greek: καινὸς δ’ ὁ σπόγγος αὐτὸς καθ’ ἑαυτὸν οὐχ ὡς ἔριον ἢ μοτὸς τιλτὸς, ὕλη μόνον ἐστὶ τῶν ἐπιβρεχομένων ὑγρῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ξηραίνει σαφῶς.
beads.english: New sponge, in and of itself, is not, like wool or a plucked lint-pledget (μοτὸς τιλτός), merely a material for the liquids poured upon it, but also dries manifestly.

beads.greek: εἴσῃ δὲ χρησάμενος ἐπὶ τραύματος αὐτῷ μόνῳ μεθ’ ὕδατος ἢ ὀξυκράτου ἢ οἴνου κατὰ τὰς τῶν σωμάτων διαφορὰς, ὡς προείρηται, κολλήσει γὰρ αὐτὰ παραπλησίως τοῖς ἐναίμοις ὀνομαζομένοις φαρμάκοις.
beads.english: You will know this if you use it on a wound by itself with water or oxykraton (vinegar-and-water) or wine, according to the differences of bodies, as has been said before; for it will glue them together much like the drugs called enaima (those for bloody wounds).

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ μὴ καινὸς, ἀλλ’ ἀπὸ χρήσεως εἴη, γνώσῃ σαφῶς ὅσον ἀπολείπεται τοῦ καινοῦ κατὰ τραυμάτων ἐπιτιθέμενος εἴτ’ οὖν ὕδατι βεβρεγμένος εἴτ’ οἴνῳ εἴτ’ ὀξυκράτῳ.
beads.english: But if it is not new but has been in use, you will clearly recognise how far it falls short of the new one when applied to wounds, whether soaked in water or in wine or in oxykraton (vinegar-and-water).

beads.greek: καὶ οὐδὲν θαυμαστὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ καινοῦ σπόγγου, διασωζομένης ἔτι τῆς δυνάμεως ἣν ἐκ τῆς θαλάττης εἶχε, ξηραίνεσθαι μετρίως τὰ σώματα.
beads.english: And there is nothing surprising in the fact that, in the case of new sponge, while the power it had from the sea is still preserved, bodies are moderately dried.

beads.greek: ταῦτα δὲ δύναται ποιεῖν, ὅταν ἔτι διασώζῃ τὴν ἀπὸ τῆς θαλάττης ὀσμὴν, ὡς ἔν γε τῷ χρόνῳ, κᾂν μηδέπω πρὸς χρῆσιν ἠγμένος ᾖ, τήν τ’ ὀσμὴν ἀπόλλυσι καὶ ξηραίνειν ὁμοίως οὐ δύναται.
beads.english: It is able to do these things so long as it still preserves the smell from the sea, since with time, even if it has not yet been brought into use, it loses its smell and is likewise unable to dry.

greek_sentences: Περὶ σπόγγου.] Σπόγγος ὁ μὲν κεκαυμένος δριμείας ἐστὶ καὶ διαφορητικῆς δυνάμεως.

ἐχρῆτο δ’ αὐτῷ τις τῶν ἡμετέρων διδασκάλων καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐν ταῖς χειρουργίαις αἱμοῤῥαγίας, ἕτοιμον ἔχων ξηρὸν μὲν καὶ ἄνικμον, δεδευμένον δὲ μάλιστα μὲν ἀσφάλτῳ, μὴ παρούσης δὲ ταύτης πίττῃ, προσετίθει δ’ αὐτὸν τοῖς αἱμοῤῥαγοῦσι χωρίοις, ἔτι καιόμενον, ὡς ἐσχαροῦσθαί τε ἅμα τὸ μόριον καὶ οἷον πῶμά τι λαμβάνειν αὐτὸ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ καυθέντος σπόγγου.
καινὸς δ’ ὁ σπόγγος αὐτὸς καθ’ ἑαυτὸν οὐχ ὡς ἔριον ἢ μοτὸς τιλτὸς, ὕλη μόνον ἐστὶ τῶν ἐπιβρεχομένων ὑγρῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ξηραίνει σαφῶς.
εἴσῃ δὲ χρησάμενος ἐπὶ τραύματος αὐτῷ μόνῳ μεθ’ ὕδατος ἢ ὀξυκράτου ἢ οἴνου κατὰ τὰς τῶν σωμάτων διαφορὰς, ὡς προείρηται, κολλήσει γὰρ αὐτὰ παραπλησίως τοῖς ἐναίμοις ὀνομαζομένοις φαρμάκοις.
εἰ δὲ μὴ καινὸς, ἀλλ’ ἀπὸ χρήσεως εἴη, γνώσῃ σαφῶς ὅσον ἀπολείπεται τοῦ καινοῦ κατὰ τραυμάτων ἐπιτιθέμενος εἴτ’ οὖν ὕδατι βεβρεγμένος εἴτ’ οἴνῳ εἴτ’ ὀξυκράτῳ.
καὶ οὐδὲν θαυμαστὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ καινοῦ σπόγγου, διασωζομένης ἔτι τῆς δυνάμεως ἣν ἐκ τῆς θαλάττης εἶχε, ξηραίνεσθαι μετρίως τὰ σώματα.
ταῦτα δὲ δύναται ποιεῖν, ὅταν ἔτι διασώζῃ τὴν ἀπὸ τῆς θαλάττης ὀσμὴν, ὡς ἔν γε τῷ χρόνῳ, κᾂν μηδέπω πρὸς χρῆσιν ἠγμένος ᾖ, τήν τ’ ὀσμὴν ἀπόλλυσι καὶ ξηραίνειν ὁμοίως οὐ δύναται.
english_sentences: On sponge.] Sponge, when burnt, is of a pungent and dispersing power.

One of our teachers used it also for the haemorrhages that occur in surgical operations, keeping it ready, dry and devoid of moisture, soaked preferably in asphalt, or, if this was not at hand, in pitch; and he applied it to the bleeding places while it was still burning, so that the part was at once made to form an eschar and the body of the burnt sponge itself was received as a kind of stopper.
New sponge, in and of itself, is not, like wool or a plucked lint-pledget (μοτὸς τιλτός), merely a material for the liquids poured upon it, but also dries manifestly.

You will know this if you use it on a wound by itself with water or oxykraton (vinegar-and-water) or wine, according to the differences of bodies, as has been said before; for it will glue them together much like the drugs called enaima (those for bloody wounds).

But if it is not new but has been in use, you will clearly recognise how far it falls short of the new one when applied to wounds, whether soaked in water or in wine or in oxykraton (vinegar-and-water).
And there is nothing surprising in the fact that, in the case of new sponge, while the power it had from the sea is still preserved, bodies are moderately dried.
It is able to do these things so long as it still preserves the smell from the sea, since with time, even if it has not yet been brought into use, it loses its smell and is likewise unable to dry.

beads.greek: Περὶ γάρου.] Γάρος δυνάμεώς ἐστι θερμῆς ἱκανῶς καὶ ξηρᾶς, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πρὸς τὰ σηπεδονώδη τῶν ἑλκῶν ἐχρήσαντό τινες αὐτῷ τῶν ἰατρῶν, ἐνιᾶσί τε τοῖς δυσεντερικοῖς τε καὶ ἰσχιαδικοῖς.
beads.english: On garum.] Garum is of a sufficiently hot and dry power, and for this reason some of the physicians have used it for the putrefactive sorts of ulcers, and they inject it both into dysenterics and into those with sciatica.

greek_sentences: Περὶ γάρου.] Γάρος δυνάμεώς ἐστι θερμῆς ἱκανῶς καὶ ξηρᾶς, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πρὸς τὰ σηπεδονώδη τῶν ἑλκῶν ἐχρήσαντό τινες αὐτῷ τῶν ἰατρῶν, ἐνιᾶσί τε τοῖς δυσεντερικοῖς τε καὶ ἰσχιαδικοῖς.
english_sentences: On garum.] Garum is of a sufficiently hot and dry power, and for this reason some of the physicians have used it for the putrefactive sorts of ulcers, and they inject it both into dysenterics and into those with sciatica.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἅλμης.] Ἅλμη τῶν ταριχηρῶν ἰχθύων ὁμοίως τῷ γάρῳ πρός τε τὰς σηπεδόνας ἁρμόζει καὶ πρὸς ἰσχιάδας καὶ δυσεντερίαν ἐνιεμένη, τῇ δὲ δριμύτητι τοὺς μὲν τὸ ἰσχίον ἐνοχλοῦντας χυμοὺς ἐπισπᾶται καὶ διὰ τῶν ἐντέρων ἐκκενοῖ, τὰ δὲ σηπεδονώδη τῶν ἑλκῶν ἐν τῇ δυσεντερίᾳ περικλύζει τε καὶ ξηραίνει.
beads.english: On brine.] The brine of salted fish, like garum, is suitable both for putrefactions and, when injected, for cases of sciatica and dysentery; by its pungency it draws out the humours troubling the hip-joint and empties them out through the intestines, while in dysentery it washes around and dries the putrefactive ulcers.

beads.greek: μάλιστα δὲ τῇ τῶν ταριχηρῶν σιλούρων καὶ τῇ τῶν μαινίδων ἅλμῃ πρὸς τὰ τοιαῦτα κέχρηνταί τινες ἰατροὶ, καὶ ἡμεῖς δ’ ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν στόματι σηπεδονωδῶν ἑλκῶν ἐχρησάμεθα.
beads.english: Some physicians have used especially the brine of salted silouroi and that of maenides for such conditions, and we too have used it on putrefactive ulcers in the mouth.

greek_sentences: Περὶ ἅλμης.] Ἅλμη τῶν ταριχηρῶν ἰχθύων ὁμοίως τῷ γάρῳ πρός τε τὰς σηπεδόνας ἁρμόζει καὶ πρὸς ἰσχιάδας καὶ δυσεντερίαν ἐνιεμένη, τῇ δὲ δριμύτητι τοὺς μὲν τὸ ἰσχίον ἐνοχλοῦντας χυμοὺς ἐπισπᾶται καὶ διὰ τῶν ἐντέρων ἐκκενοῖ, τὰ δὲ σηπεδονώδη τῶν ἑλκῶν ἐν τῇ δυσεντερίᾳ περικλύζει τε καὶ ξηραίνει.
μάλιστα δὲ τῇ τῶν ταριχηρῶν σιλούρων καὶ τῇ τῶν μαινίδων ἅλμῃ πρὸς τὰ τοιαῦτα κέχρηνταί τινες ἰατροὶ, καὶ ἡμεῖς δ’ ἐπὶ τῶν ἐν στόματι σηπεδονωδῶν ἑλκῶν ἐχρησάμεθα.
english_sentences: On brine.] The brine of salted fish, like garum, is suitable both for putrefactions and, when injected, for cases of sciatica and dysentery; by its pungency it draws out the humours troubling the hip-joint and empties them out through the intestines, while in dysentery it washes around and dries the putrefactive ulcers.
Some physicians have used especially the brine of salted silouroi and that of maenides for such conditions, and we too have used it on putrefactive ulcers in the mouth.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἀβροτόνου τε καὶ ἀψινθίου καὶ τῶν ἑκατέρου εἰδῶν.] Ἀβροτόνου ταύτης τῆς πόας οὔτε τὴν ἰδέαν χρὴ γράφειν ἐπὶ τοσούτοις τε καὶ τοιούτοις ἀνδράσιν οὔτε τὰς κατὰ μέρος ἐνεργείας ὡς ἐκεῖνοι, κᾂν εἰ μὴ διωρισμένως, ἀλλὰ σαφῶς γοῦν ἐδήλωσαν.
beads.english: On southernwood and wormwood and the species of each.] Of southernwood, this herb, one need not describe the form, after so many men of such quality, nor its particular actions, since those men set them out, if not with precise distinctions, at least clearly.

beads.greek: εἰρήσεται δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν ἐπιπλέον ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ περὶ συνθέσεως φαρμάκων πραγματείᾳ καὶ τῇ τῶν εὐπορίστων, ἔστι δ’ ὅτε κᾀν τοῖς τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου γράμμασιν, ὅταν ἡ χρεία καλῇ.
beads.english: More will also be said by us about them in the treatise on the composition of drugs and in that on easily procured remedies, and sometimes also in the writings of the Therapeutic Method, when need calls.

beads.greek: μόνον δὲ, ὅπερ ἐξ ἀρχῆς πρόκειται, τὰς καθόλου δυνάμεις ἁπάντων τῶν φαρμάκων ἐπισκέψασθαι, τοῦτο κᾀπὶ τῶν ἄλλων μὲν ἕπεται, καὶ νῦν δὲ ἤδη ποιητέον αὐτὸ καὶ λεκτέον ὡς θερμόν τέ ἐστι καὶ ξηρὸν τὴν δύναμιν τὸ ἀβρότονον, ἐν τρίτῃ που τάξει καὶ ἀποστάσει μετὰ τὰς συμμετρίας τεταγμένον, διαφορητικήν τέ τινα καὶ τμητικὴν ἔχον δύναμιν.
beads.english: Only what was proposed from the beginning, to examine the universal powers of all drugs, follows in the case of the others too, and it must now already be done here. It must be said that southernwood is hot and dry in power, ranked somewhere in the third order and remove beyond the balanced state, and has a certain dispersing and cutting power.

beads.greek: τῆς αὐτῆς δ’ ἐστὶ δυνάμεως καὶ ἡ τρίψις αὐτοῦ εἰληφυῖα, ὥσπερ τὸ σαρκωτικόν τε καὶ δακνῶδες.
beads.english: Of the same power also is its rubbing (?) having taken [it] (τρίψις … εἰληφυῖα), as also the flesh-forming and the biting.

beads.greek: ὅτι δὲ καὶ ὡς πρὸς τὴν εὔκρατον φύσιν ἡ τοιαύτη τάξις ἐξετάζεται πρόσθεν εἴρηται πολλάκις.
beads.english: That such an order is assessed relative to the well-tempered nature has often been said before.

beads.greek: ἐξεύρομεν δ’ αὐτοῦ τὴν κρᾶσιν οὐχ ἥκιστα μὲν καὶ τῇ γεύσει τεκμηράμενοι, πικρὸν γὰρ ἱκανῶς ἐστιν.
beads.english: We found out its mixture not least by judging also from taste, for it is quite bitter.

beads.greek: ὁ δὲ τοιοῦτος χυμὸς ἐδείκνυτο γεώδης μὲν ὢν τὴν οὐσίαν, ὑπὸ θερμότητος δαψιλοῦς λεπτύνεσθαι, ὥστε καὶ θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν οὐκ ἀγεννῶς.
beads.english: Such a flavour was shown to be earthy in its substance and to be thinned by abundant heat, so as both to heat and to dry not feebly.

beads.greek: οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ τῇ διωρισμένῃ πείρᾳ, περὶ ἧς ἔμπροσθεν εἴρηται πολλάκις, ἀκριβῶς βασανίσαντες ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς εὕρομεν τὸ φάρμακον τοῦτο κράσεως.
beads.english: Moreover, having tested it accurately also by the qualified experience, about which it has often been said before, we found this drug to be of the same mixture.

beads.greek: εἴτε γὰρ κόψας τὴν κόμην ἅμα τοῖς ἄνθεσιν, ἄχρηστον γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸ λοιπὸν κάρφος, ἐπιπάττοις ἕλκει καθαρῷ, δακνῶδές τε καὶ ἐρεθιστικὸν φαίνεται, εἴτε ἀποβρέξας ἐν ἐλαίῳ καταντλεῖν ἐθελήσαις ἤτοι κεφαλὴν ἢ γαστέρα, θερμαῖνον σφοδρῶς εὑρεθήσεται.
beads.english: For if you pound the foliage together with the flowers (for the rest of it, the dry stalk, is useless) and sprinkle it on a clean ulcer, it appears biting and irritant; and if you steep it in oil and choose to pour it over either the head or the belly, it will be found to heat strongly.

beads.greek: καὶ μὲν δὴ καὶ ὅσοι κατὰ περιόδους ἁλίσκονται ῥίγεσιν, εἰ καὶ τούτους ἀνατρίβοις πρὸ τῆς εἰσβολῆς, ἧττον ῥιγῶσιν, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ τὴν αἴσθησιν εὐθὺς ἅμα τῷ προσφέρεσθαι λανθάνει θερμαῖνον.
beads.english: And indeed those who are seized by rigors at periods, if you rub them down with it before the onset, shiver less; nor does it escape perception, immediately as it is applied, that it heats.

beads.greek: ὅτι δὲ ἕλμινθας ἀναιρεῖν εἰκός ἐστι πικρὸν ὑπάρχον αὐτὸ καὶ πρὸ τῆς πείρας εὔδηλον, εἴ τι μεμνήμεθα τῶν ἐν τῷ τετάρτῳ τῶνδε τῶν ὑπομνημάτων εἰρημένων ὑπὲρ τοῦ πικροῦ χυμοῦ τῆς φύσεως.
beads.english: That it is likely to destroy worms, being bitter, is clear even before experience, if we remember anything of what was said in the fourth of these commentaries about the nature of the bitter flavour.

beads.greek: εἰδήσεις δ’ εὐθὺς ὡς καὶ διαφορητικήν τινα καὶ τμητικὴν ἔχει δύναμιν.
beads.english: You will know at once that it also has a certain dispersing and cutting power.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ καὶ ὡς μᾶλλον ἀψινθίου τοῦτο ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖον αὐτῷ συλλογίσασθαί σοι παρέσται πρῶτον μὲν ἐκ τῆς γεύσεως.
beads.english: And that this must belong to it more than to wormwood you will be able to infer, first from the taste.

beads.greek: ἐλαχίστης γάρ τινος μετέχει στρυφνότητος τὸ ἀβρότονον, ἀψίνθιον δὲ οὐκ ὀλίγης· ἔπειτα δὲ κᾀκ τοῦ κακοστόμαχον εἶναι τὸ ἀβρότονον, ὥσπερ οὖν καὶ τὸ σέριφον, εὐστόμαχον δὲ τὸ ἀψίνθιον.
beads.english: For southernwood partakes of a very small acerbity, but wormwood of not a little; and then also from the fact that southernwood is bad for the stomach, as is seriphon too, whereas wormwood is good for the stomach.

beads.greek: ἐδείχθη γὰρ καὶ περὶ τούτων πρόσθεν ὡς τὸ μὲν πικρὸν αὐτὸ καθ’ αὑτὸ παντελῶς εἴη κακοστόμαχον, τὸ δὲ αὐστηρὸν ἢ στρυφνὸν ἢ ὅλως στῦφον εὐστόμαχον. ἐπιμιγνυμένων δὲ τῶν ποιοτήτων ἀλλήλαις ἡ σφοδροτέρα ἂν ἐπικρατοίη.
beads.english: For it was shown earlier about these things too that the bitter by itself is wholly bad for the stomach, whereas the harsh or acerbic or, in general, the astringent is good for the stomach; and when the qualities are mixed with one another, the stronger would prevail.

beads.greek: ταῦτ’ οὖν ἀρκεῖ σοι γινώσκειν ἐν τῇδε τῇ πραγματείᾳ.
beads.english: This, then, is enough for you to know in this treatise.

beads.greek: δειχθήσεται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου γράμμασιν ὡς ἄν τις τοιούτῳ φαρμάκῳ κάλλιστα χρῷτο.
beads.english: For it will be shown in the writings of the Therapeutic Method how one may best use such a drug.

beads.greek: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο μηκέτι ἐπιζήτει ἀκούειν μήθ’ ὅτι σὺν ἑφθῷ μήλῳ κυδονίῳ καταπλασθὲν ἢ ἄρτῳ φλεγμονὰς ὀφθαλμῶν ἰᾶται, μήθ’ ὅτι διαφορεῖ φύματα σὺν ὠμηλύσει λεῖον ἑψηθέν.
beads.english: And for this reason do not seek any longer to hear either that, applied as a poultice with boiled quince or with bread, it heals inflammations of the eyes, or that, boiled smooth with ōmēlysis, it disperses phymata.

beads.greek: οὐδὲ γὰρ τούτων οὐδέτερον οὔτε τῶν ἄλλων οὐδὲν τῆς νῦν πραγματείας ἴδιόν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ τοῖς μὲν ἐμπειρικὴν διδασκαλίαν ποιουμένοις ἐν τοῖς εὐπορίστοις γράφεται φαρμάκοις, ὅσοι δὲ λογικῶς ἀσκῆσαι τὴν τέχνην βούλονται, τῆς θεραπευτικῆς ἐστι χρεία τούτοις μεθόδου.
beads.english: For neither of these nor any of the others is proper to the present treatise; rather, for those who give an empirical teaching it is written in the easily procured drugs, while those who wish to practise the art rationally have need of the Therapeutic Method.

beads.greek: τά τε γὰρ ἄλλα καὶ βλαβείη τις ἂν μᾶλλον ἢ ὠφεληθείη πρὸς τῆς τοιαύτης ἱστορίας.
beads.english: For, among other things, one would be harmed rather than benefited by such a report.

beads.greek: Ἱπποκράτει μὲν οὖν ἐν ἀφορισμοῖς γράφοντι, ὀδύνας ὀφθαλμῶν ἀκρατοποσίη ἢ λουτρὸν ἢ πυρίη ἢ φλεβοτομίη ἢ φαρμακείη λύει· μὴ μέντοι προστιθέντι, ποίας μὲν οὖν ὀδύνας ἀκρατοποσία, ποίας δὲ λουτρὸν, καὶ τίνας μὲν πυρία, τίνας δὲ φλεβοτομία, τίνας δὲ φαρμακεία, συγχωρήσειεν ἄν τις, οἶμαι, διὰ τρεῖς αἰτίας.
beads.english: Now Hippocrates, writing in the Aphorisms, 'pains of the eyes are resolved by drinking of unmixed wine, or a bath, or a vapour-bath, or venesection, or purging', yet not adding what kind of pains drinking of unmixed wine resolves, what kind a bath, which a vapour-bath, which venesection, which purging, one would pardon, I think, for three reasons.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ ἀφοριστικὴν ἐποιεῖτο διδασκαλίαν, ἐν ᾗ διὰ τὸ σύντομον οὕτω λέγεσθαι συγκεχώρηκε τὰ πολλὰ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἰατικὰ τῶν ὀδυνῶν ἔγραψεν, εἰ καὶ μὴ διωρίσατο πρὸς ὁποίαν ὀδύνην ποῖον αὐτῶν ἁρμόττει, ἢ καὶ πολλαχόθι τῶν ἄλλων συγγραμμάτων ἀφορμὰς ἡμῖν ἔδωκε τῶν ἐν τοῖς οὕτω ῥηθεῖσι διορισμῶν.
beads.english: For he was giving an aphoristic teaching, in which, because of brevity, many things are allowed to be stated in this way; and he wrote down all the remedies of the pains, even if he did not distinguish which of them suits which kind of pain; or else in many places of his other writings he has given us starting-points for the distinctions in what was stated in this way.

beads.greek: ὅσοι δὲ μήτ’ ἐν ἑτέροις βιβλίοις ἔγραψαν ὑπὲρ τῶν τοιούτων ἀφορισμῶν μήτε ἐν διεξοδικῇ τε καὶ μακρᾷ πραγματείᾳ, γράφουσιν ἀφοριστικῶς τε καὶ βραχέως, εἴτε τὸ πρὸς τούτοις ἓν ἐκ πολλῶν δηλοῦσιν, εἰς πλείω δὲ βλάπτουσιν ἡμᾶς ἢ ὠφελοῦσι.
beads.english: But those who have written about such aphorisms neither in other books nor in a detailed and long treatise, but write aphoristically and briefly, and besides this (εἴτε τὸ πρὸς τούτοις) indicate one thing out of many, harm us in more cases than they help.

beads.greek: πολλῶν γὰρ οὐσῶν διαφορῶν ἐν ταῖς ὀφθαλμίαις, καὶ μιᾶς μὲν ἐξ αὐτῶν χρῃζούσης τοῦ προειρημένου καταπλάσματος, τῶν δ’ ἄλλων βλαπτομένων, ὁ χρώμενος ἐπὶ πασῶν ἀδιορίστως πολὺ πλείους βλάψει ἢ ὠφελήσει.
beads.english: For since there are many differentiae among ophthalmias, and one of them requires the aforementioned poultice while the others are harmed by it, he who uses it on all of them without distinction will harm many more than he helps.

beads.greek: κατὰ τοῦτον οὖν τὸν τρόπον οὐ περὶ ἀβροτόνου μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁπάντων γραπτέον ἡμῖν ἐστι, τὰς μὲν κατὰ τὸ θερμαίνειν καὶ ψύχειν ἢ ὑγραίνειν ἢ ξηραίνειν δυνάμεις ἐξ ὧν πολλάκις εἴρηκα μεθόδων εὑρίσκουσιν, ὅσα δὲ κατὰ τὴν ἰδιότητα τῆς ὅλης οὐσίας ἀποτελοῦνται τῇ πείρᾳ μόνῃ.
beads.english: In this manner, then, we must write not about southernwood alone but about all the others as well, the powers relating to heating and cooling or moistening or drying being found (εὑρίσκουσιν) by the methods I have often spoken of, but whatever is effected by the peculiarity of the whole substance by experience alone.

beads.greek: δέδεικται καὶ περὶ τῶν τοιούτων ὡς δηλητήριοί τέ εἰσι καὶ δηλητηρίων ἀλεξητήριοι καὶ καθαρτικοί.
beads.english: It has been shown about such things too that they are deleterious, and protective against deleterious things, and purgative.

beads.greek: τούτων γὰρ οὐχ οἷόν τε λογικὴν ποιήσασθαι τὴν εὕρεσιν, ἀλλ’ ἤ μόνον ὑπόνοιάν τινα πιθανὴν ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ἐπί τινων· οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἐπὶ πάντων γε, καθάπερ καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο δεδήλωται διὰ τῶν ἔμπροσθεν.
beads.english: For of these it is not possible to make a rational discovery; rather, it is only possible to find in some cases a certain plausible conjecture, and not indeed in all, just as this very point has been made clear in what precedes.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τῶν οὕτως εὑρισκομένων δυνάμεων ἰδίᾳ ποιήσομαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τοῖς ἐφεξῆς, ἐπειδὰν πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν κατὰ τὸ θερμαίνειν καὶ ψύχειν, ὑγραίνειν τε καὶ ξηραίνειν, καὶ ὅσα ταύταις ἕπονται διέλθω καθ’ ἕκαστον εἶδος φαρμάκου.
beads.english: But about the powers found in this way I shall give an account separately in what follows, once I have first gone through, for each species of drug, what concerns heating and cooling, moistening and drying, and whatever follows on these.

beads.greek: τοσόνδε μέντοι προσθεὶς ἔτι περὶ ἀβροτόνου καταπαύσω τὸν λόγον, ὡς ὁ θαυμασιώτατος Πάμφιλος, καίτοι ταύτην πρώτην πόαν γράφων καὶ τάχ’ ἂν εἰ μηδενὸς τῶν ἐφεξῆς, ἀλλὰ ταύτης γοῦν ἐθελήσας αὐτόπτης γενέσθαι, ὅμως ἔσφαλται μέγιστα, νομίζων ὑπὸ Ῥωμαίων σαντόνικον ὀνομάζεσθαι τὴν βοτάνην.
beads.english: Having added this much more about southernwood, however, I shall end the discussion: that the most admirable Pamphilus, although writing of this as his first herb, and having perhaps wished, if of none of the following, at least of this one to become an eyewitness, nevertheless erred most greatly, believing that the plant is called santonicum by the Romans.

beads.greek: διαφέρει γὰρ ἀβρότονον σαντονίκου, καθότι καὶ Διοσκουρίδης ἔγραψεν ἐν τῷ τρίτῳ περὶ ὕλης ἀκριβέστατα, καὶ πάντες ἴσασι τοῦτό γε ἰατροὶ καὶ ῥωποπῶλαι.
beads.english: For southernwood differs from santonicum, as Dioscorides too wrote most accurately in the third book On Materials, and all physicians and dealers in small wares (ῥωποπῶλαι) know this at least.

beads.greek: τοῦ μὲν γὰρ ἀβροτόνου δύο ἐστὶν εἴδη, τὸ μὲν ἄῤῥεν, τὸ δὲ θῆλυ νομιζόμενον, ὡς καὶ τοῦτο διώρισται παρὰ τῷ Διοσκουρίδῃ τε καὶ τῷ Παμφίλῳ καὶ ἄλλοις μυρίοις.
beads.english: For of southernwood there are two species, one considered male, the other female, as this too has been distinguished by Dioscorides and Pamphilus and countless others.

beads.greek: ἕτερον δέ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀψίνθιον, οὗ πάλιν εἴδη χρὴ τίθεσθαι καὶ αὐτὰ τριττὰ, ὧν τὸ μὲν τῷ γένει ὁμωνύμως προσαγορεύονται ἀψίνθιον, ὁποῖον μάλιστά ἐστι τὸ Ποντικὸν, τὸ δὲ σέριφον, τὸ δὲ σαντόνικον.
beads.english: Different from it is wormwood, of which again one must posit species, and these threefold: of which one is called wormwood, homonymously with the genus, of which kind especially is the Pontic, another seriphon, another santonicum.

beads.greek: εἰ δ’ ἄλλο μὲν ἀψίνθιον, ἄλλο δὲ σέριφον, ἄλλο δὲ σαντόνικον λέγοι, οὐδὲν εἰς τὰ παρόντα διαφέρει.
beads.english: But if one should say that wormwood is one thing, seriphon another, and santonicum another, it makes no difference for present purposes.

beads.greek: οὐδὲ γὰρ ὄνομα διαιρήσοντες ἥκομεν, ἀλλ’ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν τῶν πραγμάτων σπουδάζομεν.
beads.english: For we have not come to divide a name, but are concerned with the things themselves.

beads.greek: ἐπεὶ τοίνυν καὶ ταῦτα καὶ ταῖς ἰδέαις καὶ ταῖς γεύσεσι καὶ ταῖς δυνάμεσιν ἕτερα σαφῶς ἀλλήλων ἐστὶν, ὀνομαζέτω μὲν, εἰ βούλοιτό τις, ἅπαντα διὰ μιᾶς προσηγορίας, ἐκδιδασκέτω δὲ ἀκριβῶς τὰς δυνάμεις.
beads.english: Since, then, these are clearly different from one another in form, in taste and in powers, let anyone, if he wishes, name them all by a single appellation, but let him teach their powers accurately.

beads.greek: ἡμεῖς οὖν τὰς μὲν ἰδέας αὐτάρκως ἔφαμεν εἰρῆσθαι Διοσκουρίδῃ τε καὶ ἄλλοις οὐκ ὀλίγοις, ὥστ’ οὐ χρὴ γράφειν αὖθις ὅσα τοῖς πρόσθεν ὀρθῶς εἴρηται.
beads.english: We said, then, that the forms have been described adequately by Dioscorides and not a few others, so that one need not write again what was correctly said by our predecessors.

beads.greek: εἴ τι δ’ ἐν ταῖς τούτου δυνάμεσιν ἀδιόριστον ἐκεῖνοι παρέλιπον, οὗ δὴ χάριν ἐπὶ τήνδε τὴν ἔξοδον ἀφικόμην, ἐγὼ προσθεῖναι πειράσομαι.
beads.english: But if those men left anything undistinguished in the powers of this one, for the sake of which indeed I have come to this exposition (ἔξοδον), I shall try to add it.

beads.greek: τὸ μὲν ἀψίνθιον ἧττόν ἐστιν τῶν εἰρημένων θερμὸν, ὡς ἂν πλείστης μετέχων τῆς στύψεως.
beads.english: Wormwood is less hot than those mentioned, inasmuch as it partakes of the most astringency.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ καὶ τοῦτο λεπτομερὲς ἧττον ἐκείνων, καὶ λεπτυντικὸν δὴ κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον ἧττον ἐκείνων, οὐ μὴν ἧττόν γε ξηραντικόν.
beads.english: And if it is also less fine-particled than those, it is then in the same way also less thinning than those, yet not less drying.

beads.greek: τῶν δ’ ἄλλων τὸ μὲν σαντόνικον ἀπὸ Σαντονείας χώρας, ἐν ᾗ φύεται, τὴν προσηγορίαν ἔχον ἐγγυτάτω τὴν δύναμίν ἐστι τοῦ σερίφου, βραχεῖ τινι λειπόμενον ἐν τῷ λεπτύνειν τε καὶ θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν.
beads.english: Of the others, santonicum, which has its appellation from the Santonian country in which it grows, is nearest in power to seriphon, falling short by a little in thinning, heating and drying.

beads.greek: αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ σέριφον ἧττον μὲν θερμὸν τοῦ ἀβροτόνου, θερμότερον δὲ ἀψινθίου, κακοστόμαχον δὲ ἱκανῶς καὶ ὡς ἂν ἁλμυρίδα τινὰ σὺν πικρότητι ἀποφαῖνον, ἔτι τε τῆς στρυφνότητος ὀλίγον μετέχον.
beads.english: Seriphon itself is less hot than southernwood but hotter than wormwood, and quite bad for the stomach, as presenting a certain saltiness together with bitterness, and it further partakes a little of acerbity.

beads.greek: οὕτω δὲ καὶ ἀβρότονον καὶ σαντόνικον ἱκανῶς ἐστι κακοστόμαχον.
beads.english: So too southernwood and santonicum are quite bad for the stomach.

beads.greek: μόνον γὰρ ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ ἀψίνθιον καὶ μάλιστα τὸ Ποντικὸν εὐστόμαχόν ἐστιν ὅτι πλείστης μετέχει στύψεως.
beads.english: For among them wormwood alone, and especially the Pontic, is good for the stomach, because it partakes of the most astringency.

beads.greek: ἀβρότονον δὲ κεκαυμένον θερμὸν καὶ ξηρόν ἐστι τὴν δύναμιν, ἔτι μᾶλλον κολοκύνθης ξηρᾶς κεκαυμένης καὶ ἀνήθου ῥίζης.
beads.english: Burnt southernwood is hot and dry in power, even more so than burnt dry gourd and dill root.

beads.greek: ἐκεῖνα γὰρ ἕλκεσιν ὑγροῖς τε ἅμα καὶ χωρὶς φλεγμονῆς τετυλωμένοις ἁρμόττει, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο μάλιστα τοῖς ἐπὶ πόσθαις αἰδοίου συμπεφωνηκέναι δοκεῖ.
beads.english: For those suit ulcers that are moist and at the same time calloused without inflammation, and for this reason they seem to be especially in accord with those on the prepuce of the genitals.

beads.greek: τοῦ δὲ ἀβροτόνου ἡ τέφρα δακνώδης ἅπασιν ἕλκεσιν ὑπάρχει.
beads.english: But the ash of southernwood is biting to all ulcers.

beads.greek: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ πρὸς ἀλωπεκίας ἁρμόττει σὺν ἐλαίῳ λεπτομερεῖ, κικίνῳ δηλονότι ἢ ῥαφανίνῳ ἢ Σικυωνίῳ ἢ παλαιῷ, καὶ μάλιστα τῷ Σαβίνῳ.
beads.english: And for this reason it suits alopeciae, with a fine-particled oil, namely castor oil or radish oil or Sicyonian or old oil, and especially the Sabine.

beads.greek: καὶ γένεια δὲ βραδέως ἀνιόντα προκαλεῖται μετά τινος τῶν εἰρημένων ἐλαίων ὅτου δὴ, καὶ οὐδὲν δ’ ἧττον ἐκείνων σχινίνῳ δευόμενον.
beads.english: It also calls forth beards that are slow to come up, with any one of the oils mentioned, and no less than with those when moistened with mastic oil.

beads.greek: ἀραιωτικὸν γάρ ἐστι πρὸς τῷ λεπτομερὲς εἶναι καὶ δακνῶδες καὶ θερμὸν, ἃς δὴ καὶ μάλιστα χρὴ γινώσκειν τὰς δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ καὶ μηδὲν ἔτι τῶν κατὰ μέρος ἐν τῇδε τῇ πραγματείᾳ δεῖσθαι.
beads.english: For it is rarefying, besides being fine-particled, biting and hot; and these are the powers of it that one must especially know, and needs nothing further of the particulars in this treatise.

greek_sentences: Περὶ ἀβροτόνου τε καὶ ἀψινθίου καὶ τῶν ἑκατέρου εἰδῶν.] Ἀβροτόνου ταύτης τῆς πόας οὔτε τὴν ἰδέαν χρὴ γράφειν ἐπὶ τοσούτοις τε καὶ τοιούτοις ἀνδράσιν οὔτε τὰς κατὰ μέρος ἐνεργείας ὡς ἐκεῖνοι, κᾂν εἰ μὴ διωρισμένως, ἀλλὰ σαφῶς γοῦν ἐδήλωσαν.
εἰρήσεται δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν ἐπιπλέον ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ περὶ συνθέσεως φαρμάκων πραγματείᾳ καὶ τῇ τῶν εὐπορίστων, ἔστι δ’ ὅτε κᾀν τοῖς τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου γράμμασιν, ὅταν ἡ χρεία καλῇ.

μόνον δὲ, ὅπερ ἐξ ἀρχῆς πρόκειται, τὰς καθόλου δυνάμεις ἁπάντων τῶν φαρμάκων ἐπισκέψασθαι, τοῦτο κᾀπὶ τῶν ἄλλων μὲν ἕπεται, καὶ νῦν δὲ ἤδη ποιητέον αὐτὸ καὶ λεκτέον ὡς θερμόν τέ ἐστι καὶ ξηρὸν τὴν δύναμιν τὸ ἀβρότονον, ἐν τρίτῃ που τάξει καὶ ἀποστάσει μετὰ τὰς συμμετρίας τεταγμένον, διαφορητικήν τέ τινα καὶ τμητικὴν ἔχον δύναμιν.
τῆς αὐτῆς δ’ ἐστὶ δυνάμεως καὶ ἡ τρίψις αὐτοῦ εἰληφυῖα, ὥσπερ τὸ σαρκωτικόν τε καὶ δακνῶδες.
ὅτι δὲ καὶ ὡς πρὸς τὴν εὔκρατον φύσιν ἡ τοιαύτη τάξις ἐξετάζεται πρόσθεν εἴρηται πολλάκις.
ἐξεύρομεν δ’ αὐτοῦ τὴν κρᾶσιν οὐχ ἥκιστα μὲν καὶ τῇ γεύσει τεκμηράμενοι, πικρὸν γὰρ ἱκανῶς ἐστιν.
ὁ δὲ τοιοῦτος χυμὸς ἐδείκνυτο γεώδης μὲν ὢν τὴν οὐσίαν, ὑπὸ θερμότητος δαψιλοῦς λεπτύνεσθαι, ὥστε καὶ θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν οὐκ ἀγεννῶς.
οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ τῇ διωρισμένῃ πείρᾳ, περὶ ἧς ἔμπροσθεν εἴρηται πολλάκις, ἀκριβῶς βασανίσαντες ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς εὕρομεν τὸ φάρμακον τοῦτο κράσεως.

εἴτε γὰρ κόψας τὴν κόμην ἅμα τοῖς ἄνθεσιν, ἄχρηστον γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸ λοιπὸν κάρφος, ἐπιπάττοις ἕλκει καθαρῷ, δακνῶδές τε καὶ ἐρεθιστικὸν φαίνεται, εἴτε ἀποβρέξας ἐν ἐλαίῳ καταντλεῖν ἐθελήσαις ἤτοι κεφαλὴν ἢ γαστέρα, θερμαῖνον σφοδρῶς εὑρεθήσεται.
καὶ μὲν δὴ καὶ ὅσοι κατὰ περιόδους ἁλίσκονται ῥίγεσιν, εἰ καὶ τούτους ἀνατρίβοις πρὸ τῆς εἰσβολῆς, ἧττον ῥιγῶσιν, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ τὴν αἴσθησιν εὐθὺς ἅμα τῷ προσφέρεσθαι λανθάνει θερμαῖνον.
ὅτι δὲ ἕλμινθας ἀναιρεῖν εἰκός ἐστι πικρὸν ὑπάρχον αὐτὸ καὶ πρὸ τῆς πείρας εὔδηλον, εἴ τι μεμνήμεθα τῶν ἐν τῷ τετάρτῳ τῶνδε τῶν ὑπομνημάτων εἰρημένων ὑπὲρ τοῦ πικροῦ χυμοῦ τῆς φύσεως.
εἰδήσεις δ’ εὐθὺς ὡς καὶ διαφορητικήν τινα καὶ τμητικὴν ἔχει δύναμιν.
ἀλλὰ καὶ ὡς μᾶλλον ἀψινθίου τοῦτο ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖον αὐτῷ συλλογίσασθαί σοι παρέσται πρῶτον μὲν ἐκ τῆς γεύσεως.
ἐλαχίστης γάρ τινος μετέχει στρυφνότητος τὸ ἀβρότονον, ἀψίνθιον δὲ οὐκ ὀλίγης· ἔπειτα δὲ κᾀκ τοῦ κακοστόμαχον εἶναι τὸ ἀβρότονον, ὥσπερ οὖν καὶ τὸ σέριφον, εὐστόμαχον δὲ τὸ ἀψίνθιον.
ἐδείχθη γὰρ καὶ περὶ τούτων πρόσθεν ὡς τὸ μὲν πικρὸν αὐτὸ καθ’ αὑτὸ παντελῶς εἴη κακοστόμαχον, τὸ δὲ αὐστηρὸν ἢ στρυφνὸν ἢ ὅλως στῦφον εὐστόμαχον.
ἐπιμιγνυμένων δὲ τῶν ποιοτήτων ἀλλήλαις ἡ σφοδροτέρα ἂν ἐπικρατοίη.
ταῦτ’ οὖν ἀρκεῖ σοι γινώσκειν ἐν τῇδε τῇ πραγματείᾳ.
δειχθήσεται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς τῆς θεραπευτικῆς μεθόδου γράμμασιν ὡς ἄν τις τοιούτῳ φαρμάκῳ κάλλιστα χρῷτο.
καὶ διὰ τοῦτο μηκέτι ἐπιζήτει ἀκούειν μήθ’ ὅτι σὺν ἑφθῷ μήλῳ κυδονίῳ καταπλασθὲν ἢ ἄρτῳ φλεγμονὰς ὀφθαλμῶν ἰᾶται, μήθ’ ὅτι διαφορεῖ φύματα σὺν ὠμηλύσει λεῖον ἑψηθέν.

οὐδὲ γὰρ τούτων οὐδέτερον οὔτε τῶν ἄλλων οὐδὲν τῆς νῦν πραγματείας ἴδιόν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ τοῖς μὲν ἐμπειρικὴν διδασκαλίαν ποιουμένοις ἐν τοῖς εὐπορίστοις γράφεται φαρμάκοις, ὅσοι δὲ λογικῶς ἀσκῆσαι τὴν τέχνην βούλονται, τῆς θεραπευτικῆς ἐστι χρεία τούτοις μεθόδου.
τά τε γὰρ ἄλλα καὶ βλαβείη τις ἂν μᾶλλον ἢ ὠφεληθείη πρὸς τῆς τοιαύτης ἱστορίας.

Ἱπποκράτει μὲν οὖν ἐν ἀφορισμοῖς γράφοντι, ὀδύνας ὀφθαλμῶν ἀκρατοποσίη ἢ λουτρὸν ἢ πυρίη ἢ φλεβοτομίη ἢ φαρμακείη λύει· μὴ μέντοι προστιθέντι, ποίας μὲν οὖν ὀδύνας ἀκρατοποσία, ποίας δὲ λουτρὸν, καὶ τίνας μὲν πυρία, τίνας δὲ φλεβοτομία, τίνας δὲ φαρμακεία, συγχωρήσειεν ἄν τις, οἶμαι, διὰ τρεῖς αἰτίας.

καὶ γὰρ ἀφοριστικὴν ἐποιεῖτο διδασκαλίαν, ἐν ᾗ διὰ τὸ σύντομον οὕτω λέγεσθαι συγκεχώρηκε τὰ πολλὰ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἰατικὰ τῶν ὀδυνῶν ἔγραψεν, εἰ καὶ μὴ διωρίσατο πρὸς ὁποίαν ὀδύνην ποῖον αὐτῶν ἁρμόττει, ἢ καὶ πολλαχόθι τῶν ἄλλων συγγραμμάτων ἀφορμὰς ἡμῖν ἔδωκε τῶν ἐν τοῖς οὕτω ῥηθεῖσι διορισμῶν.

ὅσοι δὲ μήτ’ ἐν ἑτέροις βιβλίοις ἔγραψαν ὑπὲρ τῶν τοιούτων ἀφορισμῶν μήτε ἐν διεξοδικῇ τε καὶ μακρᾷ πραγματείᾳ, γράφουσιν ἀφοριστικῶς τε καὶ βραχέως, εἴτε τὸ πρὸς τούτοις ἓν ἐκ πολλῶν δηλοῦσιν, εἰς πλείω δὲ βλάπτουσιν ἡμᾶς ἢ ὠφελοῦσι.
πολλῶν γὰρ οὐσῶν διαφορῶν ἐν ταῖς ὀφθαλμίαις, καὶ μιᾶς μὲν ἐξ αὐτῶν χρῃζούσης τοῦ προειρημένου καταπλάσματος, τῶν δ’ ἄλλων βλαπτομένων, ὁ χρώμενος ἐπὶ πασῶν ἀδιορίστως πολὺ πλείους βλάψει ἢ ὠφελήσει.

κατὰ τοῦτον οὖν τὸν τρόπον οὐ περὶ ἀβροτόνου μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁπάντων γραπτέον ἡμῖν ἐστι, τὰς μὲν κατὰ τὸ θερμαίνειν καὶ ψύχειν ἢ ὑγραίνειν ἢ ξηραίνειν δυνάμεις ἐξ ὧν πολλάκις εἴρηκα μεθόδων εὑρίσκουσιν, ὅσα δὲ κατὰ τὴν ἰδιότητα τῆς ὅλης οὐσίας ἀποτελοῦνται τῇ πείρᾳ μόνῃ.
δέδεικται καὶ περὶ τῶν τοιούτων ὡς δηλητήριοί τέ εἰσι καὶ δηλητηρίων ἀλεξητήριοι καὶ καθαρτικοί.
τούτων γὰρ οὐχ οἷόν τε λογικὴν ποιήσασθαι τὴν εὕρεσιν, ἀλλ’ ἤ μόνον ὑπόνοιάν τινα πιθανὴν ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ἐπί τινων· οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἐπὶ πάντων γε, καθάπερ καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦτο δεδήλωται διὰ τῶν ἔμπροσθεν.

ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τῶν οὕτως εὑρισκομένων δυνάμεων ἰδίᾳ ποιήσομαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τοῖς ἐφεξῆς, ἐπειδὰν πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν κατὰ τὸ θερμαίνειν καὶ ψύχειν, ὑγραίνειν τε καὶ ξηραίνειν, καὶ ὅσα ταύταις ἕπονται διέλθω καθ’ ἕκαστον εἶδος φαρμάκου.

τοσόνδε μέντοι προσθεὶς ἔτι περὶ ἀβροτόνου καταπαύσω τὸν λόγον, ὡς ὁ θαυμασιώτατος Πάμφιλος, καίτοι ταύτην πρώτην πόαν γράφων καὶ τάχ’ ἂν εἰ μηδενὸς τῶν ἐφεξῆς, ἀλλὰ ταύτης γοῦν ἐθελήσας αὐτόπτης γενέσθαι, ὅμως ἔσφαλται μέγιστα, νομίζων ὑπὸ Ῥωμαίων σαντόνικον ὀνομάζεσθαι τὴν βοτάνην.
διαφέρει γὰρ ἀβρότονον σαντονίκου, καθότι καὶ Διοσκουρίδης ἔγραψεν ἐν τῷ τρίτῳ περὶ ὕλης ἀκριβέστατα, καὶ πάντες ἴσασι τοῦτό γε ἰατροὶ καὶ ῥωποπῶλαι.
τοῦ μὲν γὰρ ἀβροτόνου δύο ἐστὶν εἴδη, τὸ μὲν ἄῤῥεν, τὸ δὲ θῆλυ νομιζόμενον, ὡς καὶ τοῦτο διώρισται παρὰ τῷ Διοσκουρίδῃ τε καὶ τῷ Παμφίλῳ καὶ ἄλλοις μυρίοις.
ἕτερον δέ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀψίνθιον, οὗ πάλιν εἴδη χρὴ τίθεσθαι καὶ αὐτὰ τριττὰ, ὧν τὸ μὲν τῷ γένει ὁμωνύμως προσαγορεύονται ἀψίνθιον, ὁποῖον μάλιστά ἐστι τὸ Ποντικὸν, τὸ δὲ σέριφον, τὸ δὲ σαντόνικον.
εἰ δ’ ἄλλο μὲν ἀψίνθιον, ἄλλο δὲ σέριφον, ἄλλο δὲ σαντόνικον λέγοι, οὐδὲν εἰς τὰ παρόντα διαφέρει.
οὐδὲ γὰρ ὄνομα διαιρήσοντες ἥκομεν, ἀλλ’ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν τῶν πραγμάτων σπουδάζομεν.
ἐπεὶ τοίνυν καὶ ταῦτα καὶ ταῖς ἰδέαις καὶ ταῖς γεύσεσι καὶ ταῖς δυνάμεσιν ἕτερα σαφῶς ἀλλήλων ἐστὶν, ὀνομαζέτω μὲν, εἰ βούλοιτό τις, ἅπαντα διὰ μιᾶς προσηγορίας, ἐκδιδασκέτω δὲ ἀκριβῶς τὰς δυνάμεις.
ἡμεῖς οὖν τὰς μὲν ἰδέας αὐτάρκως ἔφαμεν εἰρῆσθαι Διοσκουρίδῃ τε καὶ ἄλλοις οὐκ ὀλίγοις, ὥστ’ οὐ χρὴ γράφειν αὖθις ὅσα τοῖς πρόσθεν ὀρθῶς εἴρηται.
εἴ τι δ’ ἐν ταῖς τούτου δυνάμεσιν ἀδιόριστον ἐκεῖνοι παρέλιπον, οὗ δὴ χάριν ἐπὶ τήνδε τὴν ἔξοδον ἀφικόμην, ἐγὼ προσθεῖναι πειράσομαι.
τὸ μὲν ἀψίνθιον ἧττόν ἐστιν τῶν εἰρημένων θερμὸν, ὡς ἂν πλείστης μετέχων τῆς στύψεως.
εἰ δὲ καὶ τοῦτο λεπτομερὲς ἧττον ἐκείνων, καὶ λεπτυντικὸν δὴ κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον ἧττον ἐκείνων, οὐ μὴν ἧττόν γε ξηραντικόν.
τῶν δ’ ἄλλων τὸ μὲν σαντόνικον ἀπὸ Σαντονείας χώρας, ἐν ᾗ φύεται, τὴν προσηγορίαν ἔχον ἐγγυτάτω τὴν δύναμίν ἐστι τοῦ σερίφου, βραχεῖ τινι λειπόμενον ἐν τῷ λεπτύνειν τε καὶ θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν.
αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ σέριφον ἧττον μὲν θερμὸν τοῦ ἀβροτόνου, θερμότερον δὲ ἀψινθίου, κακοστόμαχον δὲ ἱκανῶς καὶ ὡς ἂν ἁλμυρίδα τινὰ σὺν πικρότητι ἀποφαῖνον, ἔτι τε τῆς στρυφνότητος ὀλίγον μετέχον.
οὕτω δὲ καὶ ἀβρότονον καὶ σαντόνικον ἱκανῶς ἐστι κακοστόμαχον.
μόνον γὰρ ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ ἀψίνθιον καὶ μάλιστα τὸ Ποντικὸν εὐστόμαχόν ἐστιν ὅτι πλείστης μετέχει στύψεως.
ἀβρότονον δὲ κεκαυμένον θερμὸν καὶ ξηρόν ἐστι τὴν δύναμιν, ἔτι μᾶλλον κολοκύνθης ξηρᾶς κεκαυμένης καὶ ἀνήθου ῥίζης.
ἐκεῖνα γὰρ ἕλκεσιν ὑγροῖς τε ἅμα καὶ χωρὶς φλεγμονῆς τετυλωμένοις ἁρμόττει, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο μάλιστα τοῖς ἐπὶ πόσθαις αἰδοίου συμπεφωνηκέναι δοκεῖ.
τοῦ δὲ ἀβροτόνου ἡ τέφρα δακνώδης ἅπασιν ἕλκεσιν ὑπάρχει.
καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ πρὸς ἀλωπεκίας ἁρμόττει σὺν ἐλαίῳ λεπτομερεῖ, κικίνῳ δηλονότι ἢ ῥαφανίνῳ ἢ Σικυωνίῳ ἢ παλαιῷ, καὶ μάλιστα τῷ Σαβίνῳ.
καὶ γένεια δὲ βραδέως ἀνιόντα προκαλεῖται μετά τινος τῶν εἰρημένων ἐλαίων ὅτου δὴ, καὶ οὐδὲν δ’ ἧττον ἐκείνων σχινίνῳ δευόμενον.
ἀραιωτικὸν γάρ ἐστι πρὸς τῷ λεπτομερὲς εἶναι καὶ δακνῶδες καὶ θερμὸν, ἃς δὴ καὶ μάλιστα χρὴ γινώσκειν τὰς δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ καὶ μηδὲν ἔτι τῶν κατὰ μέρος ἐν τῇδε τῇ πραγματείᾳ δεῖσθαι.
english_sentences: On southernwood and wormwood and the species of each.] Of southernwood, this herb, one need not describe the form, after so many men of such quality, nor its particular actions, since those men set them out, if not with precise distinctions, at least clearly.

More will also be said by us about them in the treatise on the composition of drugs and in that on easily procured remedies, and sometimes also in the writings of the Therapeutic Method, when need calls.
Only what was proposed from the beginning, to examine the universal powers of all drugs, follows in the case of the others too, and it must now already be done here.
It must be said that southernwood is hot and dry in power, ranked somewhere in the third order and remove beyond the balanced state, and has a certain dispersing and cutting power.
Of the same power also is its rubbing (?) having taken [it] (τρίψις … εἰληφυῖα), as also the flesh-forming and the biting.
That such an order is assessed relative to the well-tempered nature has often been said before.
We found out its mixture not least by judging also from taste, for it is quite bitter.
Such a flavour was shown to be earthy in its substance and to be thinned by abundant heat, so as both to heat and to dry not feebly.
Moreover, having tested it accurately also by the qualified experience, about which it has often been said before, we found this drug to be of the same mixture.

For if you pound the foliage together with the flowers (for the rest of it, the dry stalk, is useless) and sprinkle it on a clean ulcer, it appears biting and irritant; and if you steep it in oil and choose to pour it over either the head or the belly, it will be found to heat strongly.
And indeed those who are seized by rigors at periods, if you rub them down with it before the onset, shiver less; nor does it escape perception, immediately as it is applied, that it heats.
That it is likely to destroy worms, being bitter, is clear even before experience, if we remember anything of what was said in the fourth of these commentaries about the nature of the bitter flavour.
You will know at once that it also has a certain dispersing and cutting power.
And that this must belong to it more than to wormwood you will be able to infer, first from the taste.

For southernwood partakes of a very small acerbity, but wormwood of not a little; and then also from the fact that southernwood is bad for the stomach, as is seriphon too, whereas wormwood is good for the stomach.

For it was shown earlier about these things too that the bitter by itself is wholly bad for the stomach, whereas the harsh or acerbic or, in general, the astringent is good for the stomach; and when the qualities are mixed with one another, the stronger would prevail.
This, then, is enough for you to know in this treatise.
For it will be shown in the writings of the Therapeutic Method how one may best use such a drug.

And for this reason do not seek any longer to hear either that, applied as a poultice with boiled quince or with bread, it heals inflammations of the eyes, or that, boiled smooth with ōmēlysis, it disperses phymata.

For neither of these nor any of the others is proper to the present treatise; rather, for those who give an empirical teaching it is written in the easily procured drugs, while those who wish to practise the art rationally have need of the Therapeutic Method.
For, among other things, one would be harmed rather than benefited by such a report.

Now Hippocrates, writing in the Aphorisms, 'pains of the eyes are resolved by drinking of unmixed wine, or a bath, or a vapour-bath, or venesection, or purging', yet not adding what kind of pains drinking of unmixed wine resolves, what kind a bath, which a vapour-bath, which venesection, which purging, one would pardon, I think, for three reasons.

For he was giving an aphoristic teaching, in which, because of brevity, many things are allowed to be stated in this way; and he wrote down all the remedies of the pains, even if he did not distinguish which of them suits which kind of pain; or else in many places of his other writings he has given us starting-points for the distinctions in what was stated in this way.

But those who have written about such aphorisms neither in other books nor in a detailed and long treatise, but write aphoristically and briefly, and besides this (εἴτε τὸ πρὸς τούτοις) indicate one thing out of many, harm us in more cases than they help.

For since there are many differentiae among ophthalmias, and one of them requires the aforementioned poultice while the others are harmed by it, he who uses it on all of them without distinction will harm many more than he helps.

In this manner, then, we must write not about southernwood alone but about all the others as well, the powers relating to heating and cooling or moistening or drying being found (εὑρίσκουσιν) by the methods I have often spoken of, but whatever is effected by the peculiarity of the whole substance by experience alone.
It has been shown about such things too that they are deleterious, and protective against deleterious things, and purgative.

For of these it is not possible to make a rational discovery; rather, it is only possible to find in some cases a certain plausible conjecture, and not indeed in all, just as this very point has been made clear in what precedes.

But about the powers found in this way I shall give an account separately in what follows, once I have first gone through, for each species of drug, what concerns heating and cooling, moistening and drying, and whatever follows on these.

Having added this much more about southernwood, however, I shall end the discussion: that the most admirable Pamphilus, although writing of this as his first herb, and having perhaps wished, if of none of the following, at least of this one to become an eyewitness, nevertheless erred most greatly, believing that the plant is called santonicum by the Romans.
For southernwood differs from santonicum, as Dioscorides too wrote most accurately in the third book On Materials, and all physicians and dealers in small wares (ῥωποπῶλαι) know this at least.
For of southernwood there are two species, one considered male, the other female, as this too has been distinguished by Dioscorides and Pamphilus and countless others.

Different from it is wormwood, of which again one must posit species, and these threefold: of which one is called wormwood, homonymously with the genus, of which kind especially is the Pontic, another seriphon, another santonicum.
But if one should say that wormwood is one thing, seriphon another, and santonicum another, it makes no difference for present purposes.
For we have not come to divide a name, but are concerned with the things themselves.
Since, then, these are clearly different from one another in form, in taste and in powers, let anyone, if he wishes, name them all by a single appellation, but let him teach their powers accurately.
We said, then, that the forms have been described adequately by Dioscorides and not a few others, so that one need not write again what was correctly said by our predecessors.
But if those men left anything undistinguished in the powers of this one, for the sake of which indeed I have come to this exposition (ἔξοδον), I shall try to add it.
Wormwood is less hot than those mentioned, inasmuch as it partakes of the most astringency.
And if it is also less fine-particled than those, it is then in the same way also less thinning than those, yet not less drying.
Of the others, santonicum, which has its appellation from the Santonian country in which it grows, is nearest in power to seriphon, falling short by a little in thinning, heating and drying.

Seriphon itself is less hot than southernwood but hotter than wormwood, and quite bad for the stomach, as presenting a certain saltiness together with bitterness, and it further partakes a little of acerbity.
So too southernwood and santonicum are quite bad for the stomach.
For among them wormwood alone, and especially the Pontic, is good for the stomach, because it partakes of the most astringency.
Burnt southernwood is hot and dry in power, even more so than burnt dry gourd and dill root.
For those suit ulcers that are moist and at the same time calloused without inflammation, and for this reason they seem to be especially in accord with those on the prepuce of the genitals.
But the ash of southernwood is biting to all ulcers.
And for this reason it suits alopeciae, with a fine-particled oil, namely castor oil or radish oil or Sicyonian or old oil, and especially the Sabine.
It also calls forth beards that are slow to come up, with any one of the oils mentioned, and no less than with those when moistened with mastic oil.
For it is rarefying, besides being fine-particled, biting and hot; and these are the powers of it that one must especially know, and needs nothing further of the particulars in this treatise.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἄγνου ἢ λύγου.] Ἄγνος δὲ ἢ λύγος, τὸ θαμνῶδες φυτὸν, θερμὸς μέν ἐστι καὶ ξηραντικὸς κατὰ τὴν τρίτην που ἀπόστασιν, λεπτομερὴς δὲ ἱκανῶς καὶ γευόμενος δριμύς τε ἅμα καὶ στύφων ἄγνος, ἢ λύγος.
beads.english: On agnos or lygos.] Agnos or lygos, the shrubby plant, is hot and drying in about the third remove, and considerably fine-particled; and to the taste the agnos, or lygos, is pungent and at the same time astringent.

beads.greek: αὐτὰς μὲν δὴ τὰς λύγους ἀχρήστους ἔχει πρὸς ἰατρείαν, τὰ δὲ φύλλα καὶ τὸ σπέρμα ξηρὰ καὶ θερμὰ τὴν δύναμίν ἐστι καὶ κατὰ τὴν οὐσίαν λεπτομερῆ.
beads.english: Its withies (lygoi) themselves it has as useless for medical treatment, but the leaves and the seed are dry and hot in power and fine-particled in substance.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ χρωμένων οὕτω φαίνεται καὶ γευομένων δριμύ τε ἅμα καὶ ὑποστῦφόν ἐστι καὶ τὸ φύλλον καὶ τὸ ἄνθος καὶ ὁ καρπός.
beads.english: For so they appear to those who use them, and to those who taste them the leaf, the flower and the fruit are pungent and at the same time slightly astringent.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἐδώδιμος ὁ καρπὸς καὶ θερμαίνει σαφῶς μετὰ τοῦ κεφαλαλγὴς ὑπάρχειν.
beads.english: The fruit is also edible, and it plainly heats, while also being productive of headache.

beads.greek: εἰ δὲ φρυχθείη, καὶ γὰρ καὶ οὕτως ἐσθίεται μετὰ τραγημάτων, ἧττον ἅπτεται τῆς κεφαλῆς.
beads.english: But if it is roasted (for it is eaten in this way too, along with dessert-nibbles), it affects the head less.

beads.greek: ἄφυσος δὲ κατὰ γαστέρα καὶ ὁ ἄφρυκτος μὲν, ἐπὶ μᾶλλον δὲ πεφρυγμένος.
beads.english: And it is free of wind in the belly: the unroasted fruit is so, but the roasted still more.

beads.greek: ἐπέχει δὲ καὶ τὰς πρὸς ἀφροδίσια ὁρμὰς ὅ τε πεφρυγμένος καὶ ὁ ἄφρυκτος καρπὸς, καὶ τὰ φύλλα καὶ τὰ ἄνθη τοῦ θάμνου ταὐτὸ τοῦτο δύναται δρᾷν, ὥστε οὐ μόνον ἐσθιόμενα καὶ πινόμενα πρὸς ἁγνείαν πεπίστευται συντελεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑποστρωννύμενα.
beads.english: Both the roasted and the unroasted fruit also check the impulses towards sexual intercourse, and the leaves and the flowers of the shrub are able to do this same thing, so that they are believed to contribute to chastity not only when eaten and drunk, but also when strewn beneath one.

beads.greek: ταῦτ’ ἄρα καὶ τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις αἱ γυναῖκες Ἀθήνῃσιν ὑποστρωννύουσιν ἑαυταῖς ὅλον τὸν θάμνον, ἐντεῦθεν δὲ καὶ τοὔνομα αὐτῷ.
beads.english: This is why at the Thesmophoria in Athens the women strew the whole shrub beneath themselves, and from this too comes its name.

beads.greek: ἐξ ὧν ἁπάντων δῆλον, εἴ γε τῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ὑπομνήμασιν εἰρημένων μεμνήμεθα, θερμαίνειν τε ἅμα καὶ ξηραίνειν καὶ ἀφυσότατον ὑπάρχειν ἄγνον.
beads.english: From all of this it is clear, if we remember what was said in the preceding treatises, that agnos heats and at the same time dries, and is most free of wind.

beads.greek: ὅτι δὲ λεπτομερὴς ἀκριβῶς ἐστιν ἡ δύναμις αὐτοῦ τεκμήριον.
beads.english: That its power is precisely fine-particled, there is evidence.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ τὸ πρὸς κεφαλὴν. ἅπτειν οὐ διὰ πλῆθος ἀτμώδους πνεύματος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γεννωμένου μᾶλλον ἤπερ διὰ θερμότητα καὶ λεπτομέρειαν εὔλογον γίνεται.
beads.english: For its affecting the head is reasonably ascribed not to a quantity of vaporous pneuma generated by it, but rather to heat and fineness of particles.

beads.greek: εἴ περ γὰρ ἦν φυσώδους πνεύματος γεννητικὸν, ἐνεφύσησέ τε ἂν τὴν γαστέρα καὶ τὰς πρὸς ἀφροδίσια παρώξυνεν ὁρμὰς ὥσπερ εὔζωμον.
beads.english: For if it were productive of windy pneuma, it would both have inflated the belly and have roused the impulses towards sexual intercourse, as rocket does.

beads.greek: ἐπεὶ δὲ οὐ μόνον οὐ παροξύνει, ἀλλὰ καὶ καταστέλλειν πέφυκεν, εἴη ἂν κατὰ τὴν πηγάνου μάλιστα δύναμιν ἐν τῷ θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν, οὐ μὴν ἶσόν γ’ ἐστὶν αὐτῷ. βραχὺ γὰρ ἀπολείπεται κατ’ ἄμφω· καὶ γὰρ θερμαντικώτερον αὐτοῦ καὶ ξηραντικώτερόν ἐστι τὸ πήγανον.
beads.english: But since it not only does not rouse them but is by nature such as to suppress them, it would be most nearly of the power of rue in heating and drying, though it is not equal to it; for it falls a little short in both respects, rue being both more heating and more drying than it.

beads.greek: διενήνοχε δὲ καὶ τῷ τῆς ποιότητος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐπιμίκτῳ.
beads.english: It differs also in the admixture of quality and power.

beads.greek: τὸ γὰρ τοῦ ἄγνου σπέρμα καὶ οἱ βλαστοὶ στύψιν τινὰ μετρίαν ἐπεισφέρουσι.
beads.english: For the seed and the shoots of agnos bring in, besides, a certain moderate astringency.

beads.greek: τὸ δὲ πήγανον ὅταν μὲν ξηρὸν ᾖ, πικρὸν ἀκριβῶς ἐστι καὶ δριμὺ, ὅταν δὲ ὑγρὸν, ὑπόπικρον.
beads.english: Rue, on the other hand, when it is dry, is exactly bitter and pungent, and when it is moist, somewhat bitter.

beads.greek: οὐ μὴν αὐστηρόν γε ἢ στρυφνόν τι πρόσεστιν αὐτῷ, ἢ εἰ καὶ προσεῖναί τῳ δόξειεν, ἀμυδρὸν παντάπασιν οἶδ’ ὅτι δόξει, καὶ οὐδαμῶς ἶσον τῷ τοῦ ἄγνου.
beads.english: No harsh or acerbic quality, however, belongs to it; or if it should seem to anyone to belong to it, I know that it will seem altogether faint, and in no way equal to that of agnos.

beads.greek: ταῦτ’ ἄρα καὶ πρὸς ἧπαρ καὶ σπλῆνα σκληρούμενά τε καὶ ἐμφραττόμενα τὸ τοῦ ἄγνου σπέρμα μᾶλλον ἢ πήγανον ἁρμόττει.
beads.english: This is why for the liver and the spleen, when they are hardened and obstructed, the seed of agnos is more suitable than rue.

beads.greek: τῆς θεραπευτικῆς δέ ἐστιν ἤδη ταῦτα μεθόδου, ἧς τὸ μὲν μηδ’ ὅλως προσάπτεσθαι φαρμάκων δυνάμεως ἀποφαινόμενον ἀδύνατόν ἐστι, τὸ δὲ ταχέως ἀπολείποντα πάλιν ἐπανέρχεσθαι πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον ἀνδρὸς ἔργον ἂν εἴη σώφρονος.
beads.english: But these matters already belong to the therapeutic method: it is impossible, when declaring the power of drugs, not to touch upon it at all, but to leave it quickly and return again to the matter proposed would be the work of a sensible man.

beads.greek: ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον ἐπὶ τῶν ἑξῆς φαρμάκων αὐτὸ δὴ τοῦτο πρᾶξαι πειράσομαι, λέγω δὴ τὸ τὴν καθόλου δύναμιν ἔκ τινων ὀλίγων ἐναργῶν ἐπιλογισάμενος ἀποχωρεῖν τῶν κατὰ μέρος ἐνεργειῶν.
beads.english: Still more in the case of the drugs that follow I shall try to do this very thing, I mean, having inferred the general power from a few evident facts, to withdraw from the particular activities.

beads.greek: ἀρκεῖ γὰρ τοῦτο μόνον εἰς τὰ παρόντα γινώσκειν, ὡς θερμὸς μὲν καὶ ξηρὸς ἄγνος τὴν δύναμίν ἐστιν οὐ μετρίως, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὴν τρίτην που τῶν ἀποστάσεων, λεπτομερὴς δὲ ἱκανῶς.
beads.english: For for present purposes it suffices to know only this: that agnos is hot and dry in power, not moderately, but in about the third of the removes, and considerably fine-particled.

beads.greek: ὁ γὰρ ταῦτα εἰδὼς, εἶτα προσμαθὼν τὴν θεραπευτικὴν μέθοδον, αὐτὸς ἐξευρήσει πῶς μὲν καταμήνια κινήσει δι’ αὐτοῦ, πῶς δὲ τὰ σκληρυνόμενα μόρια διαφορήσει, πῶς δὲ ἄκοπον ἢ θερμαντικὸν ἄλειμμα δι’ αὐτοῦ κατασκευάσει.
beads.english: For whoever knows these things, and then learns in addition the therapeutic method, will himself discover how to move the menses by means of it, how to disperse hardened parts, and how to prepare an anti-fatigue (akopon) or heating unguent by means of it.

greek_sentences: Περὶ ἄγνου ἢ λύγου.] Ἄγνος δὲ ἢ λύγος, τὸ θαμνῶδες φυτὸν, θερμὸς μέν ἐστι καὶ ξηραντικὸς κατὰ τὴν τρίτην που ἀπόστασιν, λεπτομερὴς δὲ ἱκανῶς καὶ γευόμενος δριμύς τε ἅμα καὶ στύφων ἄγνος, ἢ λύγος.
αὐτὰς μὲν δὴ τὰς λύγους ἀχρήστους ἔχει πρὸς ἰατρείαν, τὰ δὲ φύλλα καὶ τὸ σπέρμα ξηρὰ καὶ θερμὰ τὴν δύναμίν ἐστι καὶ κατὰ τὴν οὐσίαν λεπτομερῆ.
καὶ γὰρ χρωμένων οὕτω φαίνεται καὶ γευομένων δριμύ τε ἅμα καὶ ὑποστῦφόν ἐστι καὶ τὸ φύλλον καὶ τὸ ἄνθος καὶ ὁ καρπός.
ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἐδώδιμος ὁ καρπὸς καὶ θερμαίνει σαφῶς μετὰ τοῦ κεφαλαλγὴς ὑπάρχειν.
εἰ δὲ φρυχθείη, καὶ γὰρ καὶ οὕτως ἐσθίεται μετὰ τραγημάτων, ἧττον ἅπτεται τῆς κεφαλῆς.
ἄφυσος δὲ κατὰ γαστέρα καὶ ὁ ἄφρυκτος μὲν, ἐπὶ μᾶλλον δὲ πεφρυγμένος.

ἐπέχει δὲ καὶ τὰς πρὸς ἀφροδίσια ὁρμὰς ὅ τε πεφρυγμένος καὶ ὁ ἄφρυκτος καρπὸς, καὶ τὰ φύλλα καὶ τὰ ἄνθη τοῦ θάμνου ταὐτὸ τοῦτο δύναται δρᾷν, ὥστε οὐ μόνον ἐσθιόμενα καὶ πινόμενα πρὸς ἁγνείαν πεπίστευται συντελεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑποστρωννύμενα.
ταῦτ’ ἄρα καὶ τοῖς Θεσμοφορίοις αἱ γυναῖκες Ἀθήνῃσιν ὑποστρωννύουσιν ἑαυταῖς ὅλον τὸν θάμνον, ἐντεῦθεν δὲ καὶ τοὔνομα αὐτῷ.
ἐξ ὧν ἁπάντων δῆλον, εἴ γε τῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ὑπομνήμασιν εἰρημένων μεμνήμεθα, θερμαίνειν τε ἅμα καὶ ξηραίνειν καὶ ἀφυσότατον ὑπάρχειν ἄγνον.
ὅτι δὲ λεπτομερὴς ἀκριβῶς ἐστιν ἡ δύναμις αὐτοῦ τεκμήριον.
καὶ γὰρ τὸ πρὸς κεφαλὴν.
ἅπτειν οὐ διὰ πλῆθος ἀτμώδους πνεύματος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γεννωμένου μᾶλλον ἤπερ διὰ θερμότητα καὶ λεπτομέρειαν εὔλογον γίνεται.
εἴ περ γὰρ ἦν φυσώδους πνεύματος γεννητικὸν, ἐνεφύσησέ τε ἂν τὴν γαστέρα καὶ τὰς πρὸς ἀφροδίσια παρώξυνεν ὁρμὰς ὥσπερ εὔζωμον.
ἐπεὶ δὲ οὐ μόνον οὐ παροξύνει, ἀλλὰ καὶ καταστέλλειν πέφυκεν, εἴη ἂν κατὰ τὴν πηγάνου μάλιστα δύναμιν ἐν τῷ θερμαίνειν καὶ ξηραίνειν, οὐ μὴν ἶσόν γ’ ἐστὶν αὐτῷ.
βραχὺ γὰρ ἀπολείπεται κατ’ ἄμφω· καὶ γὰρ θερμαντικώτερον αὐτοῦ καὶ ξηραντικώτερόν ἐστι τὸ πήγανον.
διενήνοχε δὲ καὶ τῷ τῆς ποιότητος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐπιμίκτῳ.
τὸ γὰρ τοῦ ἄγνου σπέρμα καὶ οἱ βλαστοὶ στύψιν τινὰ μετρίαν ἐπεισφέρουσι.
τὸ δὲ πήγανον ὅταν μὲν ξηρὸν ᾖ, πικρὸν ἀκριβῶς ἐστι καὶ δριμὺ, ὅταν δὲ ὑγρὸν, ὑπόπικρον.
οὐ μὴν αὐστηρόν γε ἢ στρυφνόν τι πρόσεστιν αὐτῷ, ἢ εἰ καὶ προσεῖναί τῳ δόξειεν, ἀμυδρὸν παντάπασιν οἶδ’ ὅτι δόξει, καὶ οὐδαμῶς ἶσον τῷ τοῦ ἄγνου.
ταῦτ’ ἄρα καὶ πρὸς ἧπαρ καὶ σπλῆνα σκληρούμενά τε καὶ ἐμφραττόμενα τὸ τοῦ ἄγνου σπέρμα μᾶλλον ἢ πήγανον ἁρμόττει.

τῆς θεραπευτικῆς δέ ἐστιν ἤδη ταῦτα μεθόδου, ἧς τὸ μὲν μηδ’ ὅλως προσάπτεσθαι φαρμάκων δυνάμεως ἀποφαινόμενον ἀδύνατόν ἐστι, τὸ δὲ ταχέως ἀπολείποντα πάλιν ἐπανέρχεσθαι πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον ἀνδρὸς ἔργον ἂν εἴη σώφρονος.
ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον ἐπὶ τῶν ἑξῆς φαρμάκων αὐτὸ δὴ τοῦτο πρᾶξαι πειράσομαι, λέγω δὴ τὸ τὴν καθόλου δύναμιν ἔκ τινων ὀλίγων ἐναργῶν ἐπιλογισάμενος ἀποχωρεῖν τῶν κατὰ μέρος ἐνεργειῶν.
ἀρκεῖ γὰρ τοῦτο μόνον εἰς τὰ παρόντα γινώσκειν, ὡς θερμὸς μὲν καὶ ξηρὸς ἄγνος τὴν δύναμίν ἐστιν οὐ μετρίως, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὴν τρίτην που τῶν ἀποστάσεων, λεπτομερὴς δὲ ἱκανῶς.

ὁ γὰρ ταῦτα εἰδὼς, εἶτα προσμαθὼν τὴν θεραπευτικὴν μέθοδον, αὐτὸς ἐξευρήσει πῶς μὲν καταμήνια κινήσει δι’ αὐτοῦ, πῶς δὲ τὰ σκληρυνόμενα μόρια διαφορήσει, πῶς δὲ ἄκοπον ἢ θερμαντικὸν ἄλειμμα δι’ αὐτοῦ κατασκευάσει.
english_sentences: On agnos or lygos.] Agnos or lygos, the shrubby plant, is hot and drying in about the third remove, and considerably fine-particled; and to the taste the agnos, or lygos, is pungent and at the same time astringent.
Its withies (lygoi) themselves it has as useless for medical treatment, but the leaves and the seed are dry and hot in power and fine-particled in substance.
For so they appear to those who use them, and to those who taste them the leaf, the flower and the fruit are pungent and at the same time slightly astringent.
The fruit is also edible, and it plainly heats, while also being productive of headache.
But if it is roasted (for it is eaten in this way too, along with dessert-nibbles), it affects the head less.
And it is free of wind in the belly: the unroasted fruit is so, but the roasted still more.

Both the roasted and the unroasted fruit also check the impulses towards sexual intercourse, and the leaves and the flowers of the shrub are able to do this same thing, so that they are believed to contribute to chastity not only when eaten and drunk, but also when strewn beneath one.
This is why at the Thesmophoria in Athens the women strew the whole shrub beneath themselves, and from this too comes its name.
From all of this it is clear, if we remember what was said in the preceding treatises, that agnos heats and at the same time dries, and is most free of wind.
That its power is precisely fine-particled, there is evidence.
For its affecting the head is reasonably ascribed not to a quantity of vaporous pneuma generated by it, but rather to heat and fineness of particles.
For if it were productive of windy pneuma, it would both have inflated the belly and have roused the impulses towards sexual intercourse, as rocket does.

But since it not only does not rouse them but is by nature such as to suppress them, it would be most nearly of the power of rue in heating and drying, though it is not equal to it; for it falls a little short in both respects, rue being both more heating and more drying than it.
It differs also in the admixture of quality and power.
For the seed and the shoots of agnos bring in, besides, a certain moderate astringency.
Rue, on the other hand, when it is dry, is exactly bitter and pungent, and when it is moist, somewhat bitter.
No harsh or acerbic quality, however, belongs to it; or if it should seem to anyone to belong to it, I know that it will seem altogether faint, and in no way equal to that of agnos.
This is why for the liver and the spleen, when they are hardened and obstructed, the seed of agnos is more suitable than rue.

But these matters already belong to the therapeutic method: it is impossible, when declaring the power of drugs, not to touch upon it at all, but to leave it quickly and return again to the matter proposed would be the work of a sensible man.
Still more in the case of the drugs that follow I shall try to do this very thing, I mean, having inferred the general power from a few evident facts, to withdraw from the particular activities.
For for present purposes it suffices to know only this: that agnos is hot and dry in power, not moderately, but in about the third of the removes, and considerably fine-particled.

For whoever knows these things, and then learns in addition the therapeutic method, will himself discover how to move the menses by means of it, how to disperse hardened parts, and how to prepare an anti-fatigue (akopon) or heating unguent by means of it.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἀγρώστεως.] Τῆς δὲ ἀγρώστεως ἡ μὲν ῥίζα συμμέτρως ἐστὶ ψυχρὰ καὶ ξηρὰ, ἔχουσά τι ὀλίγον δακνῶδες καὶ λεπτομερές.
beads.english: On agrōstis.] Of agrōstis, the root is moderately cold and dry, having a small degree of something biting and fine-particled.

beads.greek: ἡ δὲ πόα ψύχει μὲν κατὰ τὴν πρώτην ἀπόστασιν, σύμμετρος δ’ ἐστὶ κατὰ ὑγρότητα καὶ ξηρότητα.
beads.english: The herb cools at the first remove, but is moderate as regards moistness and dryness.

beads.greek: τὸ δὲ σπέρμα τῆς μὲν ἄλλης ἀσθενὲς ὑπάρχει, τῆς δ’ ἐν τῷ Παρνασσῷ ξηραντικόν τε καὶ λεπτομερὲς καὶ ὑπόστρυφνον.
beads.english: The seed of the other kind is weak, but that of the kind on Parnassus is drying, fine-particled and slightly acerbic.

beads.greek: ἄγρωστις ἐδώδιμον ἔχει τὴν ῥίζαν, ἔστ’ ἂν ᾖ μαλακὴ, γλυκεῖα μὲν ὑδατώδης, δριμὺ δέ τι καὶ ὑπόστρυφνον ὀλίγον ἔχουσα.
beads.english: Agrōstis has an edible root, as long as it is soft: it is sweet [and] watery, but has something pungent and a little slightly acerbic.

beads.greek: αὕτη δὲ ἡ πόα τελέως ἐστὶν ὑδατώδης γευομένοις.
beads.english: The herb itself is entirely watery to those who taste it.

beads.greek: ἐξ ὧν δῆλον ὡς μετρίως μέν ἐστιν ἡ ῥίζα ψυχρὰ καὶ ξηρὰ καὶ διὰ τοῦτο κολλητικὸν τῶν ἐναίμων ἑλκῶν.
beads.english: From which it is clear that the root is moderately cold and dry, and for this reason is agglutinating of bloody wounds.

beads.greek: αὐτὴ δὲ ἡ πόα καταπλασσομένη ψύχει μὲν οὐκ ἰσχυρῶς, ὑγρότητος δὲ καὶ ξηρότητος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καθέστηκε.
beads.english: The herb itself, applied as a poultice, cools, but not strongly, and stands in the middle between moistness and dryness.

beads.greek: τὸ δὲ ἐν τῇ ῥίζῃ δακνῶδες καὶ λεπτομερές ἐστι μὲν ὀλίγον, εἴωθε δ’ οὖν ἔστιν ὅτε καὶ λίθους θρύπτειν, εἴ τις αὐτὴν ἀφεψήσας πίνοι.
beads.english: The biting and fine-particled element in the root is slight, but it is nonetheless sometimes wont also to break up stones, if one boils it down and drinks it.

beads.greek: τὸ δὲ σπέρμα τῆς μὲν ἄλλης ἀσθενές ἐστιν, τῆς δ’ ἐν τῷ Παρνασσῷ διουρητικόν τέ ἐστι καὶ ῥεύματα ξηραίνει γαστρὸς καὶ στομάχου.
beads.english: The seed of the other kind is weak, but that of the kind on Parnassus is diuretic and dries fluxes of the belly and stomach.

beads.greek: δύναμις γάρ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ ξηραντική τε καὶ λεπτομερὴς καὶ ὑπόστρυφνος.
beads.english: For its power is drying, fine-particled and slightly acerbic.

english_sentences: On agrōstis.] Of agrōstis, the root is moderately cold and dry, having a small degree of something biting and fine-particled.
The herb cools at the first remove, but is moderate as regards moistness and dryness.
The seed of the other kind is weak, but that of the kind on Parnassus is drying, fine-particled and slightly acerbic.
Agrōstis has an edible root, as long as it is soft: it is sweet [and] watery, but has something pungent and a little slightly acerbic.
The herb itself is entirely watery to those who taste it.
From which it is clear that the root is moderately cold and dry, and for this reason is agglutinating of bloody wounds.
The herb itself, applied as a poultice, cools, but not strongly, and stands in the middle between moistness and dryness.
The biting and fine-particled element in the root is slight, but it is nonetheless sometimes wont also to break up stones, if one boils it down and drinks it.
The seed of the other kind is weak, but that of the kind on Parnassus is diuretic and dries fluxes of the belly and stomach.
For its power is drying, fine-particled and slightly acerbic.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἀγχούσης καὶ τεττάρων ἀγχουσῶν.] Τῆς δὲ ἀγχούσης τέταρτόν ἐστιν εἶδος, ὧν ἡ μὲν ὀνόκλεια ψύχουσαν ἱκανῶς καὶ ξηραίνουσαν ἔχει τὴν ῥίζαν, στύφουσάν τε ἅμα καὶ ὑπόπικρον, ἱκανὴν δὲ καὶ λεπτῦναι καὶ ἀποῤῥῦψαι τοὺς χολώδεις χυμοὺς καὶ πυκνῶσαι τὰ σώματα.
beads.english: On anchousa, and the four anchousai.] Of anchousa there are four kinds. Of these, onokleia has a root that cools and dries considerably, and is at once astringent and somewhat bitter, able to thin and to cleanse away the bilious humours and to condense bodies.

beads.greek: τὰ δὲ φύλλα ἀσθενέστερα μὲν ἔχει τῆς ῥίζης, στύφει δὲ αὐτὰ καὶ ξηραίνει.
beads.english: Its leaves are weaker than the root, but they too are astringent and drying.

beads.greek: καὶ ἡ λύκοψις δὲ προσαγορευομένη ψύχει μὲν καὶ ξηραίνει, ῥίζαν δ’ ἔχει στυπτικωτέραν τῆς ὀνοκλείας.
beads.english: The one called lykopsis also cools and dries, but has a root more astringent than that of onokleia.

beads.greek: ἡ δὲ ὀνόχειλος θερμοτέρα τέ ἐστι καὶ φαρμακωδεστέρα. πλέον γὰρ ἔχει καὶ πρὸς τὴν γεῦσιν εὐθὺς τὸ δριμύ.
beads.english: Onocheilos is hotter and more drug-like, for it has more of the pungent, which is evident to the taste at once.

beads.greek: ταύτης δ’ ἔτι θερμοτέρα, ἣ μικρὰ καὶ πικροτέρα καὶ πλέον ἔτι φαρμακωδεστέρα τυγχάνει.
beads.english: Hotter still than this is the one that is small, more bitter and more drug-like still.

beads.greek: ἄγχουσαι δὲ οὐ τῆς αὐτῆς ἅπασαι δυνάμεως.
beads.english: The anchousai are not all of the same power.

beads.greek: ἡ μὲν γὰρ ὀνόκλεια προσαγορευομένη στύφουσάν τε ἅμα καὶ ὑπόπικρον ἔχει τὴν ῥίζαν, ἱκανὴν καὶ πυκνῶσαι τὰ σάματα καὶ μετρίως λεπτῦναι καὶ ἀποῤῥῦψαι καὶ ἀποπλῦναι τοὺς χολώδεις καὶ ἁλμυρώδεις χυμούς.
beads.english: The one called onokleia has a root at once astringent and somewhat bitter, able to condense bodies and moderately to thin, cleanse away and wash out the bilious and salty humours.

beads.greek: ἐῤῥέθη γὰρ ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ὡς ἡ στρυφνὴ ποιότης ἐπιμεμιγμένη τῇ πικρᾷ ταῦτα ἐργάζεσθαι πέφυκεν.
beads.english: For it was said earlier that the acerbic quality, mixed with the bitter, naturally produces these effects.

beads.greek: οὕτω τέ τοι καὶ ἰκτερικοῖς καὶ σπληνικοῖς καὶ νεφριτικοῖς ὠφέλιμος ὑπάρχει.
beads.english: In this way it is beneficial to those with jaundice, to splenetics and to nephritics.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ καὶ ψύχειν μὲν ἱκανὴ καὶ καταπλασσομένη γε σὺν ἀλφίτοις ἐρυσιπέλατα ὠφελεῖ, καὶ ἀποῤῥύπτει δὲ οὐ πινομένη μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἔξωθεν ἐπιτιθεμένη, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀλφοὺς καὶ λέπρας ἰᾶται σὺν ὄξει.
beads.english: It is also able to cool, and applied as a poultice with barley-groats it helps erysipelas. It cleanses not only when drunk but also when applied externally, and for this reason it heals alphoi and leprai with vinegar.

beads.greek: τὰ μὲν τῆς ῥίζης ἔργα ταῦτα καὶ αἱ τῶν ἔργων δυνάμεις αἱ εἰρημέναι.
beads.english: These are the effects of the root, and the powers behind those effects are those stated.

beads.greek: τὰ δὲ φύλλα τῆς βοτάνης ἐστὶν μὲν ἀσθενέστερα τῆς ῥίζης, οὐκ ἀπήλλακται δὲ τοῦ ξηραίνειν τε καὶ στύφειν, ὥστε καὶ διάῤῥοιαν ἰᾶται σὺν οἴνῳ πινόμενα.
beads.english: The leaves of the plant are weaker than the root, but they are not without drying and astringency, so that, drunk with wine, they also heal diarrhoea.

beads.greek: καὶ ἡ λύκοψις δὲ προσαγορευομένη τοῖς ἐρυσιπέλασιν ὁμοίως ἁρμόζει καὶ ῥίζαν ἔχει στυπτικωτέραν τῆς ὀνοκλείας.
beads.english: The one called lykopsis is likewise suited to cases of erysipelas, and has a root more astringent than that of onokleia.

beads.greek: τῆς δὲ ὀνοχείλους τε καὶ Ἀλκιβιαδείου καλουμένης ἡ μὲν δύναμίς ἐστι φαρμακωδεστέρα.
beads.english: The power of onocheilos, also called Alkibiadeios, is more drug-like.

beads.greek: πλέον γοῦν ἔχει καὶ πρὸς τὴν γεῦσιν εὐθὺς τὸ δριμὺ καὶ ἐχιοδήκτοις ἱκανῶς ἁρμόττει καταπλαττομένη καὶ περιαπτομένη καὶ ἐσθιομένη.
beads.english: At any rate it has more of the pungent, evident to the taste at once, and it is well suited to people bitten by vipers, whether applied as a poultice, hung on as an amulet or eaten.

beads.greek: ἡ λοιπὴ δὲ τετάρτη καὶ μικρὰ καὶ σχεδὸν ἀνώνυμος ἐξ αὐτῶν μόνη, παραπλησία μέν ἐστι τῇ Ἀλκιβιαδείῳ, πικροτέρα δὲ καὶ πλέον ἐστὶ φαρμακωδεστέρα, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πρὸς τὰς πλατείας ἕλμινθας ἐπιτηδεία, πλῆθος ὀξυβάφου σὺν ὑσσώπῳ τε καὶ καρδάμῳ πινομένη.
beads.english: The remaining fourth, which is small and almost alone among them without a name, is close to the Alkibiadeios, but more bitter and still more drug-like. For this reason it is useful against flat worms, drunk in the quantity of an oxybaphon with hyssop and cress.

ταύτης δ’ ἔτι θερμοτέρα, ἣ μικρὰ καὶ πικροτέρα καὶ πλέον ἔτι φαρμακωδεστέρα τυγχάνει.
ἄγχουσαι δὲ οὐ τῆς αὐτῆς ἅπασαι δυνάμεως.
ἡ μὲν γὰρ ὀνόκλεια προσαγορευομένη στύφουσάν τε ἅμα καὶ ὑπόπικρον ἔχει τὴν ῥίζαν, ἱκανὴν καὶ πυκνῶσαι τὰ σάματα καὶ μετρίως λεπτῦναι καὶ ἀποῤῥῦψαι καὶ ἀποπλῦναι τοὺς χολώδεις καὶ ἁλμυρώδεις χυμούς.
ἐῤῥέθη γὰρ ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ὡς ἡ στρυφνὴ ποιότης ἐπιμεμιγμένη τῇ πικρᾷ ταῦτα ἐργάζεσθαι πέφυκεν.
οὕτω τέ τοι καὶ ἰκτερικοῖς καὶ σπληνικοῖς καὶ νεφριτικοῖς ὠφέλιμος ὑπάρχει.
ἔστι δὲ καὶ ψύχειν μὲν ἱκανὴ καὶ καταπλασσομένη γε σὺν ἀλφίτοις ἐρυσιπέλατα ὠφελεῖ, καὶ ἀποῤῥύπτει δὲ οὐ πινομένη μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἔξωθεν ἐπιτιθεμένη, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἀλφοὺς καὶ λέπρας ἰᾶται σὺν ὄξει.
τὰ μὲν τῆς ῥίζης ἔργα ταῦτα καὶ αἱ τῶν ἔργων δυνάμεις αἱ εἰρημέναι.
τὰ δὲ φύλλα τῆς βοτάνης ἐστὶν μὲν ἀσθενέστερα τῆς ῥίζης, οὐκ ἀπήλλακται δὲ τοῦ ξηραίνειν τε καὶ στύφειν, ὥστε καὶ διάῤῥοιαν ἰᾶται σὺν οἴνῳ πινόμενα.
καὶ ἡ λύκοψις δὲ προσαγορευομένη τοῖς ἐρυσιπέλασιν ὁμοίως ἁρμόζει καὶ ῥίζαν ἔχει στυπτικωτέραν τῆς ὀνοκλείας.
τῆς δὲ ὀνοχείλους τε καὶ Ἀλκιβιαδείου καλουμένης ἡ μὲν δύναμίς ἐστι φαρμακωδεστέρα.
πλέον γοῦν ἔχει καὶ πρὸς τὴν γεῦσιν εὐθὺς τὸ δριμὺ καὶ ἐχιοδήκτοις ἱκανῶς ἁρμόττει καταπλαττομένη καὶ περιαπτομένη καὶ ἐσθιομένη.

ἡ λοιπὴ δὲ τετάρτη καὶ μικρὰ καὶ σχεδὸν ἀνώνυμος ἐξ αὐτῶν μόνη, παραπλησία μέν ἐστι τῇ Ἀλκιβιαδείῳ, πικροτέρα δὲ καὶ πλέον ἐστὶ φαρμακωδεστέρα, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πρὸς τὰς πλατείας ἕλμινθας ἐπιτηδεία, πλῆθος ὀξυβάφου σὺν ὑσσώπῳ τε καὶ καρδάμῳ πινομένη.
english_sentences: On anchousa, and the four anchousai.] Of anchousa there are four kinds.
Of these, onokleia has a root that cools and dries considerably, and is at once astringent and somewhat bitter, able to thin and to cleanse away the bilious humours and to condense bodies.
Its leaves are weaker than the root, but they too are astringent and drying.
The one called lykopsis also cools and dries, but has a root more astringent than that of onokleia.
Onocheilos is hotter and more drug-like, for it has more of the pungent, which is evident to the taste at once.
Hotter still than this is the one that is small, more bitter and more drug-like still.
The anchousai are not all of the same power.
The one called onokleia has a root at once astringent and somewhat bitter, able to condense bodies and moderately to thin, cleanse away and wash out the bilious and salty humours.
For it was said earlier that the acerbic quality, mixed with the bitter, naturally produces these effects.
In this way it is beneficial to those with jaundice, to splenetics and to nephritics.
It is also able to cool, and applied as a poultice with barley-groats it helps erysipelas.
It cleanses not only when drunk but also when applied externally, and for this reason it heals alphoi and leprai with vinegar.
These are the effects of the root, and the powers behind those effects are those stated.
The leaves of the plant are weaker than the root, but they are not without drying and astringency, so that, drunk with wine, they also heal diarrhoea.
The one called lykopsis is likewise suited to cases of erysipelas, and has a root more astringent than that of onokleia.
The power of onocheilos, also called Alkibiadeios, is more drug-like.
At any rate it has more of the pungent, evident to the taste at once, and it is well suited to people bitten by vipers, whether applied as a poultice, hung on as an amulet or eaten.
The remaining fourth, which is small and almost alone among them without a name, is close to the Alkibiadeios, but more bitter and still more drug-like.
For this reason it is useful against flat worms, drunk in the quantity of an oxybaphon with hyssop and cress.

beads.greek: Περὶ ῥίζης ἀγαρικοῦ.] Ἀγαρικοῦ ῥίζα τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἐπιφυομένη πρέμνῳ, κατὰ μὲν τὴν πρώτην γεῦσιν γλυκεῖά τις, ὑπόπικρος δὲ ὀλίγον ὕστερον φαινομένη καί τινος ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ δριμύτητος ἔμφασιν ἐπάγουσα, καὶ βραχείας στύψεως.
beads.english: On the root of agaric.] The root of agaric, that is, the growth upon a tree-trunk, appears at the first taste somewhat sweet, but a little later somewhat bitter, and in time it brings on an impression of a certain pungency and of slight astringency.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ καὶ χαύνη τὴν σύστασιν.
beads.english: It is also loose in its consistency.

beads.greek: ἐξ ὧν ἁπάντων εὔδηλον, εἴπερ τῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ὑπομνήμασιν εἰρημένων μνημονεύομεν, ὡς σύνθετόν ἐστι τὸ φάρμακον ἐξ οὐσίας ἀερώδους τε καὶ γεώδους, ὑπὸ θερμότητος λελεπτυσμένης, ἥκιστα δὲ τῆς ὑδατώδους μετέχει.
beads.english: From all of this it is quite clear, if we remember what was said in the preceding treatises, that the drug is compounded of an airy and earthy substance thinned by heat, and has very little share in the watery substance.

beads.greek: ταῦτ’ ἄρα διαφορητικήν τε καὶ θερμαντικὴν τὴν δύναμιν ἔχει, καὶ πάχους τμητικὴν καὶ διακαθαίρει τὰς ἐν τοῖς σπλάγχνοις ἐμφράξεις, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἰκτεριῶντας ἰᾶται, τοὺς ἐπ’ ἐμφράξει τῶν καθ’ ἧπαρ οὕτω κάμνοντας.
beads.english: It therefore has a dispersing and heating power, and one that is cutting of thickness; it clears out the obstructions in the viscera, and for this reason it heals those suffering from jaundice, that is, those who are ill in this way from obstruction of the parts about the liver.

beads.greek: ὀνίνησι δὲ καὶ τοὺς ἐπιλήπτους διὰ τὴν αὐτὴν δύναμιν καὶ ῥίγη τὰ κατὰ περίοδον, ὅσα παχέων ἢ γλίσχρων ἐστὶ χυλῶν ἔγγονα, καὶ ταῦτα ἰᾶται.
beads.english: By the same power it also benefits epileptics, and it heals periodic rigors as well, those that are the offspring of thick or viscid juices.

beads.greek: ὠφελεῖ δὲ καὶ τοὺς ὑπὸ κατὰ ψύξιν ἀδικούντων θηρίων δηχθέντας, ἢ νυγέντας, ἔξωθέν τε κατὰ τοῦ πεπονθότος ἐπιτιθέμενον, εἴσω τε τοῦ σώματος λαμβάνον ὁλκῇ δραχμῆς μιᾶς μετ’ οἴνου κεκραμένου.
beads.english: It also helps those bitten or stung by wild creatures that do harm by chilling, both when it is applied externally on the affected part and when it is taken into the body in the weight of one drachm with mixed wine.

beads.greek: ἔστι δὲ καὶ καθαρτικόν.
beads.english: It is also purgative.

ἐξ ὧν ἁπάντων εὔδηλον, εἴπερ τῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν ὑπομνήμασιν εἰρημένων μνημονεύομεν, ὡς σύνθετόν ἐστι τὸ φάρμακον ἐξ οὐσίας ἀερώδους τε καὶ γεώδους, ὑπὸ θερμότητος λελεπτυσμένης, ἥκιστα δὲ τῆς ὑδατώδους μετέχει.

english_sentences: On the root of agaric.] The root of agaric, that is, the growth upon a tree-trunk, appears at the first taste somewhat sweet, but a little later somewhat bitter, and in time it brings on an impression of a certain pungency and of slight astringency.
It is also loose in its consistency.

From all of this it is quite clear, if we remember what was said in the preceding treatises, that the drug is compounded of an airy and earthy substance thinned by heat, and has very little share in the watery substance.

It therefore has a dispersing and heating power, and one that is cutting of thickness; it clears out the obstructions in the viscera, and for this reason it heals those suffering from jaundice, that is, those who are ill in this way from obstruction of the parts about the liver.
By the same power it also benefits epileptics, and it heals periodic rigors as well, those that are the offspring of thick or viscid juices.

It also helps those bitten or stung by wild creatures that do harm by chilling, both when it is applied externally on the affected part and when it is taken into the body in the weight of one drachm with mixed wine.
It is also purgative.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἀγηράτου.] Ἀγήρατόν ἐστι δυνάμεως διαφορητικῆς τε καὶ ἀτρέμα πως ἀφλεγμάντου.
beads.english: On agēraton.] Agēraton is of a power that is dispersing and also, in a gentle sort of way, anti-inflammatory.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἀδιάντου.] Τὸ δὲ ἀδίαντον κατὰ μὲν θερμότητα καὶ ψυχρότητα σύμμετρόν ἐστι, ξηραίνει δὲ καὶ λεπτύνει καὶ διαφορεῖ.
beads.english: On adiantum.] Adiantum is moderate as regards heat and cold, but it dries, thins and disperses.

beads.greek: καὶ γὰρ ἀλωπεκίας δασύνει καὶ χοιράδας καὶ ἀποστήματα διαφορεῖ καὶ λίθους θρύπτει πινόμενον, καὶ ταῖς ἐκ θώρακός τε καὶ πνεύμονος ἀναγωγαῖς τῶν γλίσχρων καὶ παχέων χυμῶν οὐ σμικρὰ συντελεῖ, καὶ ῥεῦμα κοιλίας ἵστησιν.
beads.english: For it makes alopeciae grow hair again, disperses choirades and abscessions, breaks up stones when drunk, contributes not a little to the bringing up of viscous and thick humours from the chest and lung, and stops a flux of the belly.

beads.greek: οὐ μὴν θερμότητά γέ τινα προσβάλλει σαφῆ, καθάπερ οὐδὲ ψύξιν.
beads.english: Yet it does not impart any manifest heat, just as it does not impart any manifest cooling either.

beads.greek: ἀλλὰ θείη τις ἂν αὐτὸ κατὰ τὴν ἐν τούτοις ἀντίθεσίν τε καὶ κρᾶσιν ἐν τῇ μέσῃ τάξει.
beads.english: Rather, one might place it in the middle rank with respect to the opposition and mixture of these qualities.

Περὶ ἀδιάντου.] Τὸ δὲ ἀδίαντον κατὰ μὲν θερμότητα καὶ ψυχρότητα σύμμετρόν ἐστι, ξηραίνει δὲ καὶ λεπτύνει καὶ διαφορεῖ.

καὶ γὰρ ἀλωπεκίας δασύνει καὶ χοιράδας καὶ ἀποστήματα διαφορεῖ καὶ λίθους θρύπτει πινόμενον, καὶ ταῖς ἐκ θώρακός τε καὶ πνεύμονος ἀναγωγαῖς τῶν γλίσχρων καὶ παχέων χυμῶν οὐ σμικρὰ συντελεῖ, καὶ ῥεῦμα κοιλίας ἵστησιν.

ἀλλὰ θείη τις ἂν αὐτὸ κατὰ τὴν ἐν τούτοις ἀντίθεσίν τε καὶ κρᾶσιν ἐν τῇ μέσῃ τάξει.
english_sentences: On agēraton.] Agēraton is of a power that is dispersing and also, in a gentle sort of way, anti-inflammatory.
On adiantum.] Adiantum is moderate as regards heat and cold, but it dries, thins and disperses.

For it makes alopeciae grow hair again, disperses choirades and abscessions, breaks up stones when drunk, contributes not a little to the bringing up of viscous and thick humours from the chest and lung, and stops a flux of the belly.
Yet it does not impart any manifest heat, just as it does not impart any manifest cooling either.
Rather, one might place it in the middle rank with respect to the opposition and mixture of these qualities.

beads.greek: Περὶ ἀειζώου.] Ἀείζωον ἑκάτερον, καὶ τὸ μικρὸν καὶ τὸ μέγα, ξηραίνει μὲν ἐπ’ ὀλίγον, ὅτι καὶ στύφει μετρίως, ἀπηλλαγμένον ἁπάσης ἄλλης ἰσχυρᾶς ποιότητος, ὡς ἐπικρατεῖν ἐν αὐτῷ τὴν ὑδατώδη μᾶλλον οὐσίαν· ἐμψύχει δὲ οὐ μετρίως.
beads.english: On aeizoon.] Each kind of aeizoon, both the small and the large, dries to a slight degree, because it is also moderately astringent, while being free of every other strong quality, so that in it the watery substance rather predominates; but it cools to no moderate degree.

beads.greek: ἔστι γὰρ τῆς τρίτης ἀποστάσεώς τε καὶ τάξεως τῶν ψυχόντων.
beads.english: For it belongs to the third remove and order of cooling things.

beads.greek: ταῦτ’ ἄρα καὶ πρὸς ἐρυσιπέλατα μὲν, ἀλλὰ καὶ πρὸς ἕρπητας καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἐκ ῥευμάτων φλεγμονὰς ἁρμόττει.
beads.english: For this reason it is suitable for erysipelas, and also for herpēs and for the inflammations that arise from fluxes.
